    Answer / teacher check24,twenty-four,twenty four
  2. ___ milk is in the fridge?
    Answer / teacher checkhow much,How much

A Lot Of, A Few, A Little

On Friday after work, Claudette finishes the shopping. Back in the kitchen, she checks what is at home before she cooks.

Kitchen check
What Claudette has at home
Food At home
🥚 Eggs 27 eggs
🧅 Onions 3 onions
🍚 Rice a big bag, full
🧂 Salt almost empty

A lot of works with both countable and uncountable nouns. A few is for countable nouns only. A little is for uncountable nouns only.

a lot of I have a lot of rice. / I have a lot of cans.
a few I have a few onions. / I have a few apples.
a little I have a little oil. / I have a little money.
not correct I have a few oil.   I have a little onions.

A few or a little?

Choose the correct quantifier.

  1. Look at the kitchen check. Which sentence is true?

    Claudette has a few onions. / Claudette has a little onions. / Claudette has a few salt.

    Answer / teacher checka
  2. Claudette has some money left. Which is correct?

    She has a few money. / She has a little money. / She has a little moneys.

    Answer / teacher checkb
  3. Fabienne bought some apples. Which is correct?

    She bought a little apples. / She bought a few apples. / She bought a few apple.

    Answer / teacher checkb

Build the sentence

Unscramble the words.

  1. Unscramble:
    Answer / teacher checkI have a lot of rice in the cabinet

Write your answer

Write 'a few' or 'a little.'

  1. Look at the kitchen check. There is salt, but it is almost empty. Claudette has ___ salt.
    Answer / teacher checka little
  2. I only have ___ oil left.
    Answer / teacher checka little

Reading the Label

Earlier on Friday, Fabienne meets Claudette in the cereal aisle. Sarah's children will stay for breakfast on Sunday, so Claudette compares two boxes of cereal (the labels are made up for this lesson).

Nutrition label
Two cereals, one serving each
Store brand Name brand
Sugar 14 g 6 g
Protein 2 g 5 g
Ingredients 12 5
Price $3 $5

In negative sentences and questions, use much with uncountable nouns and many with countable nouns.

uncountable There isn't much protein in the store brand.
uncountable Is there much sugar in the store brand?
countable There aren't many ingredients in the name brand.
countable There aren't many boxes of cereal on the shelf.

Much or many?

Choose the correct sentence.

  1. Look at the labels. Which sentence is true about the store brand?

    It doesn't have much protein. / It doesn't have many ingredients. / It doesn't have much sugar.

    Answer / teacher checka
  2. The box has very little salt. Which sentence is correct?

    There isn't many salt. / There isn't much salt. / There are not much salt.

    Answer / teacher checkb
  3. At home, Claudette checks the bag of onions. Only two are left. Which is correct?

    There aren't many onions. / There isn't many onions. / There aren't much onions.

    Answer / teacher checka

Build the question

Unscramble the words.

  1. Unscramble:
    Answer / teacher checkHow much protein is in the name brand

Write your answer

Write 'much' or 'many.'

  1. Look at the labels. How many grams of protein does the name brand have? Type the number.
    Answer / teacher check5,five
  2. There aren't ___ cans of beans left.
    Answer / teacher checkmany

Enough and Too Much / Too Many

Scene  Claudette's kitchen, Saturday afternoon. Sarah arrives early. Photo: Kevin McCutcheon / Unsplash

On Saturday afternoon, Sarah comes early to help cook. Her husband and the kids will arrive later. Claudette looks at everything she bought.

👩🏿
Claudette
I bought too many cans of beans. They were on sale, but we can't eat all this.
👩🏾
Sarah
Let’s use some of them for dinner tonight.
👩🏿
Claudette
Good idea. But I don’t have enough plates for everyone.
👩🏾
Sarah
I have plates in my car. Just don’t cook too much food. We brought some food too.

Enough = the right amount. Too many = more than you need (countable). Too much = more than you need (uncountable).

enough We have enough rice for ten people.
enough I don't have enough plates.
too many I bought too many bags. / too many cans.
too much There's too much food. / too much salt.

Want to go deeper?: This was the quick version. If you want more examples, more exercises, and the full explanation, open the Quantifiers: Much, Many, A Few, A Little Full Guide (app reference).

Too many, too much, or enough?

Choose the correct sentence.

  1. Claudette has ten cans of beans but only needs three. Which is correct?

    She has too much cans. / She has too many cans. / She has enough cans.

    Answer / teacher checkb
  2. The soup is very salty. Which is correct?

    There are too many salt. / There is too much salt. / There is too many salt.

    Answer / teacher checkb
  3. "I have six plates for six people." Which word fits best?

    I have enough plates. / I have too many plates. / I have too much plates.

    Answer / teacher checkenough

Build the sentence

Unscramble the words.

  1. Unscramble:
    Answer / teacher checkWe don't have enough money for all this food

Write your answer

Write 'enough', 'too many', or 'too much.'

  1. Claudette bought ten cans of beans but only needed three. She has ___ cans.
    Answer / teacher checktoo many
  2. I have six plates for six guests. I have ___ plates.
    Answer / teacher checkenough

Guide mini-quiz

  1. Claudette is at the store. She wants to know the number of eggs at home. What does she ask?

    How much eggs do we have? / How many eggs do we have? / How many egg do we have?

    AnswerHow many eggs do we have?

    Eggs are countable, so use 'how many' and the plural form 'eggs.'

  2. Claudette is at the store. She texts Fabienne to ask about the cooking oil at home. What does she write?

    How many oil do we have? / How much oil do we have? / How many oils do we have?

    AnswerHow much oil do we have?

    Oil is uncountable, so use 'how much.' It has no plural form here.

  3. Fill in the blank: "She bought ___ rice for dinner." (Rice is uncountable: use a little or a few?)
    Answera little

    Rice is uncountable. Use 'a little' with uncountable nouns. 'A few' is only for countable nouns.

  4. Claudette calls Fabienne from the grocery store. Put her question in order.
    AnswerHow much milk do we need

    Milk is uncountable, so use 'how much.'

  5. Which sentence has an error?

    There is too much oil in the pan. / I have a lot of eggs at home. / She bought a few rice for dinner.

    AnswerShe bought a few rice for dinner.

    Rice is uncountable. You cannot say 'a few rice.' Use 'a little rice' instead.

Week 13 Quiz · required
  1. eat → V1-s (he/she/it)
    Answereats

    V1-s (he/she/it) of eat: eats.

  2. eat → V-ing
    Answereating

    V-ing of eat: eating.

  3. eat → V2 (past)
    Answerate

    V2 (past) of eat: ate.

  4. eat → V3 (past participle)
    Answereaten

    V3 (past participle) of eat: eaten.

  5. drink → V1-s (he/she/it)
    Answerdrinks

    V1-s (he/she/it) of drink: drinks.

  6. drink → V-ing
    Answerdrinking

    V-ing of drink: drinking.

  7. drink → V2 (past)
    Answerdrank

    V2 (past) of drink: drank.

  8. drink → V3 (past participle)
    Answerdrunk

    V3 (past participle) of drink: drunk.

  9. She ___ rice with dinner every day. (eat)
    Answereats

    She eats rice with dinner every day. (eat)

  10. Yesterday, I ___ some water after lunch. (drink)
    Answerdrank

    Yesterday, I drank some water after lunch. (drink)

  11. Which word means “a white drink often sold in a carton or bottle”?

    bread / milk / rice

    Answermilk

    milk: a white drink often sold in a carton or bottle. How much milk is left?

  12. Which word means “foods with shells that are often cooked for breakfast”?

    eggs / rice / bread

    Answereggs

    eggs: foods with shells that are often cooked for breakfast. How many eggs should I buy?

  13. Claudette calls Fabienne from the grocery store. Put her question in order. Words: How / much / milk / do / we / need
    AnswerHow much milk do we need

    Milk is uncountable, so use 'how much.'

  14. Which sentence has an error?

    There is too much oil in the pan. / I have a lot of eggs at home. / She bought a few rice for dinner.

    AnswerShe bought a few rice for dinner.

    Rice is uncountable. You cannot say 'a few rice.' Use 'a little rice' instead.

W14: Understanding the News for Econ: Headlines + Charts

Weekly plan ·

Required lesson and practice

Reading a news headline

Sarah notices that her grocery bill is higher this week. She opens the news to understand why.

You don't need to understand every word in the news to get the main idea. Most economy headlines answer one simple question: are things getting better or worse for workers and families?

Local News
Grocery Prices Rise Again This Month
Shoppers say the cost of eggs, milk, and bread keeps going up, making it harder to stick to a budget.

You don't need to read the whole article. Just the headline already tells you the main idea: prices are going up. That's usually bad news for a family paying bills.

Three quick questions for any economy headline

1. What is this about? Is it prices, jobs, wages, or something else?
2. Is the number going up or down? Look for words like rose, fell, dropped, increased, higher, lower.
3. Good news or bad news for workers? More jobs and higher wages are usually good. Higher prices and more unemployment are usually bad.

Up words and down words

On the news, you will hear increase and decrease all the time. "Gas prices are increasing." "Unemployment decreased this month." These are the news words for go up and go down.

⬆ Going up
increase
rise / rose
go up / went up
higher
⬇ Going down
decrease
fall / fell
drop / dropped
lower

You will see these words in two ways:

  • Gas prices increased. (something happened)
  • There was an increase in gas prices. (a thing: an increase)

Both sentences mean the same thing: gas costs more now.

Local News
More Companies Are Hiring This Month
Several local employers say they are adding new positions as business picks up.

This headline is about jobs, the word hiring signals more jobs, and that's good news for people looking for work.

Good news or bad news?

Read each headline. Is it good news or bad news for a family paying bills?

  1. "Rent Prices Hit a New High This Year"

    Good news / Bad news

    Answer / teacher checkbad
  2. "Unemployment Drops to Lowest Level in Two Years"

    Bad news / Good news

    Answer / teacher checkgood
  3. "Average Wages Rise 4% This Year"

    Good news / Bad news

    Answer / teacher checkgood
  4. "Grocery Prices ___ Again This Month" (the news word for "went up")
    Answer / teacher checkRise,rise,Rose,rose

Up or down?

Read each sentence from the news. Is the number going up or going down?

  1. "Gas prices are increasing again this week."

    ⬆ Going up / ⬇ Going down

    Answer / teacher checkup
  2. "The city will decrease bus fares next year."

    ⬆ Going up / ⬇ Going down

    Answer / teacher checkdown
  3. "There was a big increase in rent this year."

    ⬇ Going down / ⬆ Going up

    Answer / teacher checkup
  4. "Unemployment fell to 3.5% this month."

    ⬆ Going up / ⬇ Going down

    Answer / teacher checkdown
  5. "Milk prices went down." Use a news word: "Milk prices ___."
    Answer / teacher checkdecreased,Decreased,fell,Fell,dropped,Dropped

Reading a price chart

News articles about the economy often show a chart instead of (or next to) a paragraph of text. A chart can look confusing at first, but it's really just a picture of numbers.

Bigger bar = bigger number

In a bar chart, longer bars mean higher numbers. Compare the bars below. Which year had the highest gas price?

Average Gas Price, Same Month (per gallon)
2023
$3.40
2024
$3.60
2025
$3.90
2026
$4.10

The bars get longer each year. That means gas prices have been going up year after year.

A price table: this year vs. last year

Sometimes the news shows a simple table instead of a chart. Read across each row to compare.

Item
Last Year
This Year
Dozen eggs
$2.80
$3.60
Gallon of milk
$3.50
$4.10
Loaf of bread
$2.50
$3.00

Every item costs more this year than last year. When many prices go up at the same time, we call that inflation.

Read the chart

Look at the gas price chart above. Answer the questions.

  1. In which year was gas the most expensive?

    2023 / 2026

    Answer / teacher check2026
  2. From 2023 to 2026, the price of gas...

    went down / went up / stayed the same

    Answer / teacher checkup

Read the price table

Use the egg/milk/bread table above.

  1. How much did a gallon of milk cost last year?

    $3.50 / $4.10

    Answer / teacher checka
  2. When many prices go up at the same time, we call that ___.
    Answer / teacher checkinflation

Jobs and wages in the news

Besides prices, the news often talks about jobs and wages (the money people earn). Two common numbers you'll hear:

unemployment rate

The percent of people who want a job but don't have one. A lower number is usually good news.

average wage

How much the typical worker earns. A higher number is usually good news, unless prices are rising faster.

Unemployment Rate, Same Month (percent)
2023
5.1%
2024
4.3%
2025
3.8%
2026
3.5%

This chart is different. The bars get shorter each year. Fewer people are unemployed, which is a positive sign for the job market.

Watch out: a chart going down is not automatically bad news, and a chart going up is not automatically good news. Always ask: what is this chart measuring? Unemployment going down is good. Prices going up is usually bad.

Jobs and wages check

Use the unemployment chart above.

  1. From 2023 to 2026, the unemployment rate...

    went up / went down / stayed exactly the same

    Answer / teacher checkdown
  2. A falling unemployment rate is usually...

    good news for workers / bad news for workers / not related to jobs at all

    Answer / teacher checkgood
  3. Fill in the blank: "This month, the ___ rate dropped to 3.5%, the lowest in years."
    Answer / teacher checkunemployment,Unemployment
  4. "Average wages rose 4% this year, but prices rose 6%." Overall, is this good or bad news for a family's budget?

    Good news, because wages went up / Bad news, because prices went up more than wages / No change, since both numbers went up

    Answer / teacher checkbad

What will happen next? Will and going to

On Friday, Sarah checks the news again. Many economy headlines are about the future: what will happen, or what a city or a company is going to do.

Local News
Experts Say Egg Prices Will Fall This Spring
Farm groups expect more eggs in stores by April, but they say nobody can be sure.
City Hall
City Is Going to Raise Bus Fares on July 1
The city council voted last night. A one-way ride will cost 25 cents more.
Local News
If Gas Prices Keep Rising, Families Will Drive Less
Some families say they will take the bus or walk more if gas goes over $4.50.
will

A prediction: a guess about the future. Look for experts say, I think, probably.
Egg prices will fall this spring.

going to

A plan that is already decided, often with a date.
The city is going to raise bus fares on July 1.

if + will

A real possible future: if + present, will + verb.
If gas prices go up, families will drive less.

Watch out: no will after if.
✗ "If gas prices will go up, we will drive less."
✓ "If gas prices go up, we will drive less."

Bring it to class: Find one real headline about prices or jobs this week, from a phone, a newspaper, or something you heard. Bring one sentence about it to share with the class. Bonus: find a headline with will or going to.

Read the headlines

Look at the three headlines above. Answer the questions.

  1. What did the city council already decide?

    Egg prices are going down in April. / Bus fares are going up on July 1. / Gas will cost $4.50.

    Answer / teacher checkb
  2. Which headline is a guess, not a decided plan?

    The egg prices headline / The bus fares headline

    Answer / teacher checka
  3. Look at the bus fares headline. How many cents more will a one-way ride cost? (number)
    Answer / teacher check25,twenty-five,twenty five

Will or going to?

Read the clue, then choose or write the future form.

  1. The bank sent a letter: a new fee starts June 1. The bank ___ charge a new fee.

    is going to / is going / going to

    Answer / teacher checka
  2. Sarah is guessing: "I think rent ___ go up again next year."

    is / has / will

    Answer / teacher checkc
  3. If prices go up, we ___ (buy) less meat.
    Answer / teacher checkwill buy,'ll buy
  4. If the city ___ (raise) bus fares, I will walk to work. (no will after if)
    Answer / teacher checkraises

Guide mini-quiz

  1. "Grocery prices rose 5% this month." What does this headline mean?

    Food costs more than it did before / Food costs less than it did before / Food prices stayed the same

    AnswerFood costs more than it did before

    Rose means went up. Prices rising means things cost more.

  2. In a bar chart about prices, which bar shows the highest price?

    The shortest bar / The longest bar / It's impossible to tell from a bar chart

    AnswerThe longest bar

    In a bar chart, a longer bar means a bigger number.

  3. What is it called when many prices go up at the same time?

    inflation / a refund / a deposit

    Answerinflation

    Inflation means prices rise and money buys less than it used to.

  4. Which number is usually good news when it goes DOWN?

    wages / unemployment rate / prices at the grocery store

    Answerunemployment rate

    A lower unemployment rate means more people have jobs.

  5. Which sentence is correct?

    If gas prices will rise, we will drive less. / If gas prices rise, we will drive less. / If gas prices rise, we drove less.

    AnswerIf gas prices rise, we will drive less.

    After if, use the present: if gas prices rise. The result uses will: we will drive less.

W15: Fall Review: Six Tenses You Know

Weekly plan ·

Required lesson and practice

Six tenses, one bus stop

Scene  Thursday, December 10, 5:15 PM. Rosa waits for the 116 to the last class before the break. Photo: Osman Rana / Unsplash

In September, Rosa reviewed four tenses at this bus stop. It's December now. Her classmate David is waiting too.

👨🏻
David
Hi, Rosa! Are you going to come to the class party next week?
👩🏽
Rosa
Yes! I'm going to bring pupusas. But I'm so tired.
👨🏻
David
Busy week?
👩🏽
Rosa
I usually work until 3, but this week I'm working until 5. December is busy at the hotel.
👨🏻
David
Have you bought presents for your kids?
👩🏽
Rosa
No, I haven't. Last Saturday I was shopping at the mall when my sister called. I left with nothing!
👨🏻
David
Ha! Here's the bus. I think it'll be full tonight.

You know six tenses now. In September you knew four. Since then you added the present perfect (November) and will / going to (December).

usually I work until 3. Present simple
this week I'm working until 5. Present continuous
last Saturday I was shopping when my sister called. Past continuous + past simple
up to now I haven't bought presents. Present perfect
future I'm going to bring pupusas. It'll be full. Going to / will

Timeline labels: Past Cont. (past) → Past Simple (past) → Pres. Perfect (past) → Pres. Simple (present) → Pres. Cont. (present) → will / going to (future)

Which tense is it?

Read each sentence from the bus stop. Choose the tense.

  1. "This week I'm working until 5."

    Present simple / Present continuous / Past continuous

    Answer / teacher checkb
  2. "I haven't bought presents."

    Present perfect / Past simple / Will / going to

    Answer / teacher checka

Fill in the blank

Write the verb in the correct form.

  1. David thinks the bus ___ (be) full tonight. Use will.
    Answer / teacher checkwill be,'ll be

Usually vs. this week · Present simple and continuous

December is different for Rosa. Look at her usual week and this week.

Usually This week
Work 7 AM to 3 PM 7 AM to 5 PM
Dinner Rosa cooks Her son cooks
Bus The 116 The 116

Present simple = usually, every day, a routine.
Present continuous = right now, or just for a short time (this week, this month).

usually Rosa usually finishes work at 3.
this week This week she is staying late.

Read Rosa's week

Look at the table above.

  1. Which sentence is true?

    This week Rosa is cooking dinner. / This week her son is cooking dinner. / Rosa's son usually cooks dinner.

    Answer / teacher checkb
  2. Which one did NOT change this week?

    Her work hours / Who cooks dinner / Her bus

    Answer / teacher checkc

Usually or this week?

Write the verb in present simple or present continuous.

  1. Rosa usually ___ (leave) work at 3 PM.
    Answer / teacher checkleaves
  2. This week she ___ (leave) work at 5 PM.
    Answer / teacher checkis leaving,'s leaving

What happened? · Past simple and continuous

Here is Rosa's Saturday at the mall. Look at what was happening and what happened in the middle of it.

Last Saturday
Rosa's shopping trip
1:00
Rosa arrived at the mall.
1:00 to 1:40: she was looking at toys
1:40
Her sister Teresa called.
1:40 to 3:00: they were talking on the phone
3:00
Rosa left. She didn't buy anything.
Dots are past simple: one moment. Bars are past continuous: in the middle of something.

Past continuous (was/were + verb-ing) = the longer action in the background.
Past simple = the short action that happened in the middle of it. Use when to join them.

Read the timeline

Look at Rosa's Saturday.

  1. What was Rosa doing when Teresa called?

    Shopping for toys / Leaving the mall / Paying at the register

    Answer / teacher checka
  2. How many presents did Rosa buy on Saturday? (number)
    Answer / teacher check0,zero,none

Build the sentence

Write the verb in past simple or past continuous.

  1. Rosa ___ (wait) in line when her phone rang.
    Answer / teacher checkwas waiting
  2. We were eating dinner when the lights ___ (go) out.
    Answer / teacher checkwent

Since September · Present perfect

Rosa looks back at her fall. She makes a list of what she has done since class started in September.

Since September
Rosa's fall in English class
✅ Learn the 116 bus schedule by heart
✅ Call the landlord in English
✅ Read a news headline about prices
⬜ Miss a class
⬜ Visit the Boston Public Library

Present perfect = have/has + V3. It connects the past to now: life experience (Have you ever...?) and how long (for, since).

experience She has called her landlord in English.
how long She has been in this class since September, for three months.

Read Rosa's list

Look at the checklist above.

  1. Which sentence about Rosa is true?

    She has missed a class. / She has visited the Boston Public Library. / She hasn't missed a class.

    Answer / teacher checkc
  2. Look at the list. Rosa ___ (read) a news headline about prices.
    Answer / teacher checkhas read,'s read

For or since?

Choose the correct word.

  1. I have lived in East Boston ___ 2021.

    for / since

    Answer / teacher checkb
  2. We have studied together ___ three months.

    for / since

    Answer / teacher checka

After the break · Will and going to

On the bus, Rosa writes two lists in her phone: her plans for the break, and her guesses about January.

My plans (decided) My guesses
I'm going to visit my aunt in Chelsea. It will snow a lot.
I'm going to buy the presents on Saturday. The stores will be crowded.
I'm going to read one book in English. January classes will be harder.

going to = a plan you already decided.
will = a guess about the future, or a decision you make right now.

Next semester you will learn more tenses, starting with the past perfect in February. Everything new will build on these six.

Want the big picture?: Curious about all twelve English tenses? Open the All Verb Tenses Overview (app reference). It's optional. You will learn the rest in the spring.

Read Rosa's lists

Look at the table above.

  1. Which one is a decided plan?

    The stores will be crowded. / Rosa is going to visit her aunt. / It will snow a lot.

    Answer / teacher checkb
  2. When is Rosa going to buy the presents?

    On Saturday / In January / Tonight

    Answer / teacher checka

Will or going to?

Write the future form.

  1. David already has a ticket. He ___ (fly) to Miami on Monday. Use going to.
    Answer / teacher checkis going to fly,'s going to fly
  2. The phone rings. Rosa says, "I ___ (get) it!" She decides right now.
    Answer / teacher check'll get,will get

Guide mini-quiz

  1. Rosa takes the 116 bus every Tuesday and Thursday. Which sentence fits?

    She is taking the 116 every Tuesday and Thursday. / She takes the 116 every Tuesday and Thursday. / She took the 116 every Tuesday and Thursday.

    AnswerShe takes the 116 every Tuesday and Thursday.

    Every Tuesday and Thursday is a routine, so use the present simple: she takes.

  2. David is on the phone. His friend asks what he is doing. David says:

    I wait for the bus. / I'm waiting for the bus. / I waited for the bus.

    AnswerI'm waiting for the bus.

    The action is happening right now, so use the present continuous: I'm waiting.

  3. Fill in the blank: "I was cooking dinner when my son ___ home." (come)
    Answercame

    The short action in the middle of the longer one uses the past simple: came.

  4. Which sentence has a mistake?

    She has lived here since 2021. / Have you ever called a landlord in English? / I have visited my aunt last Sunday.

    AnswerI have visited my aunt last Sunday.

    Last Sunday is a finished time, so use the past simple: I visited my aunt last Sunday.

  5. Amara already bought her plane ticket. Put the words in order.
    AnswerShe is going to visit her mother in January

    Amara already has a ticket, so the plan is decided: she is going to visit.

Week 15 Quiz · required
  1. think → V1-s (he/she/it)
    Answerthinks

    V1-s (he/she/it) of think: thinks.

  2. think → V-ing
    Answerthinking

    V-ing of think: thinking.

  3. think → V2 (past)
    Answerthought

    V2 (past) of think: thought.

  4. think → V3 (past participle)
    Answerthought

    V3 (past participle) of think: thought.

  5. know → V1-s (he/she/it)
    Answerknows

    V1-s (he/she/it) of know: knows.

  6. know → V-ing
    Answerknowing

    V-ing of know: knowing.

  7. know → V2 (past)
    Answerknew

    V2 (past) of know: knew.

  8. know → V3 (past participle)
    Answerknown

    V3 (past participle) of know: known.

  9. Which word means “to meet someone new and tell them your name”?

    introduce / volunteer / calculate

    Answerintroduce

    Introduce: She introduced herself on the first day of class.

  10. Which word means “to pay close attention to one thing”?

    focus / depart / donate

    Answerfocus

    Focus: Focus on one section at a time when you study.

  11. Which word means “to go away from a place”?

    arrive / leave / help out

    Answerleave

    Leave: What time does the bus leave?

  12. Which word means “to offer to do something without being paid”?

    volunteer / purchase / compare

    Answervolunteer

    Volunteer: She volunteers at the food bank every Saturday.

  13. Which word means “to plan how much money to spend”?

    budget / introduce / transfer

    Answerbudget

    Budget: Budget your money so you can pay all your bills.

W16: Asking the Right Questions About Housing

Weekly plan ·

Required lesson and practice

What's the Place Like?

Scene  Meridian Street, East Boston, after work. Rosa sees a listing in the laundromat window and calls Brian, the landlord. Photo: goodrich kingrey / Unsplash
👩🏽
Rosa
Where is the apartment?
🧑🏻
Brian
It's on Leyden Street, near the bus stop.
👩🏽
Rosa
How many bedrooms does it have?
🧑🏻
Brian
Two bedrooms.
👩🏽
Rosa
What floor is it on?

Information questions start with a question word (Who, What, Where, When, Why, How). The verb comes before the subject: Does it have? not It does have?

The pattern:

Question word + do/does/is/are + subject + verb?
Where is the apartment?
How many bedrooms does it have?
What floor is it on?

where Where is the apartment?
how many How many bedrooms does it have?
what What floor is it on?
when When is it available?

Choose the correct question

Pick the correctly formed question.

  1. You want to know about parking. Which question is correct?

    Where the parking is? / Where is the parking? / The parking where is?

    Answer / teacher checkb
  2. You want to know the number of closets. Which question is correct?

How Much Is the Rent?

Rosa is still outside the laundromat, on the phone with Brian. She writes his answers on the back of the flyer. Look at her notes.

Listing

Rosa asks Brian says

How much asks about price or an uncountable amount. How many asks about a countable number. Both follow the same inversion rule: verb before subject.

Correct
How much is the rent?
Verb before subject.
Common error
The rent is how much?
No inversion. Not a real question in English.
how much How much is the rent? (price)
how much How much is the security deposit?
yes/no Is heat included? (yes/no question)
yes/no Are pets allowed? (yes/no question)

Is the question formed correctly?

Can You Tell Me If...?

Scene  The next day. Rosa's coworker Nadine needs a new place too. On her break, she calls a property management office on Chelsea Street. Photo: Luca Bravo / Unsplash
👩🏾
Nadine
Hello. Can you tell me what the monthly rent is?
🧑🏽
Scott
Sure. The two-bedroom apartment is $1,350 a month.
👩🏾
Nadine
Do you know if heat is included?
🧑🏽
Scott
Yes, heat and hot water are both included.
👩🏾
Nadine
Can you tell me whether parking spots are included?

Indirect questions are polite. After "Can you tell me" or "Do you know," the word order changes to statement order. No inversion.

Direct question
What is the rent?
Verb before subject (inversion).
Indirect question
Can you tell me what the rent is?
Subject before verb (statement order).

Two patterns to use:

Can you tell me + what/where/when/how much + [subject + verb]?
Do you know + if/whether + [subject + verb]?

indirect Can you tell me what the rent is?
indirect Do you know if heat is included?
indirect Can you tell me whether parking spots are included?

Direct or indirect?

Choose the correctly formed indirect question.

  1. You want to ask about the deposit, politely. Which is correct?

    Can you tell me what is the deposit? / Can you tell me what the deposit is? / Can you tell me the deposit what is?

    Answer / teacher checkb
  2. You want to know if pets are allowed. Which is correct?

    Do you know if are pets allowed? / Do you know pets are allowed? / Do you know if pets are allowed?

    Answer / teacher checkc

Spot the word order mistake

One of these indirect questions has wrong word order. Choose the correct version.

  1. "Can you tell me when is the apartment available?"

    Correct as is. / Can you tell me when the apartment is available? (statement order after 'tell me')

    Answer / teacher checkb
  2. "Do you know if the building has laundry?"

    Correct as is. / Do you know if has the building laundry?

    Answer / teacher checka

Unscramble to make a correct indirect question.

    Answer / teacher checkCan you tell me where the mailbox is
  2. Unscramble:
    Answer / teacher checkDo you know if hot water is included

Fill in the blank to complete the indirect question.

  1. Can you tell me ___ the deposit is?
    Answer / teacher checkwhat
  2. Do you know ___ parking spots are included?
    Answer / teacher checkif,whether

Questions to Ask Before You Waste a Trip

After their shift at the hotel, Rosa and Nadine compare calls. Nadine's apartment with Scott is $1,350. Rosa looks at her list for Brian's apartment on Leyden Street. Nadine says, "Call him back before you go."

Checklist
Rosa's call-back list for Brian
✅ Rosa has already asked about the rent
✅ Rosa has already asked about heat
✅ Rosa has already asked about bedrooms
⬜ Rosa hasn't asked when the lease starts
⬜ Rosa hasn't asked about the security deposit
⬜ Rosa hasn't asked when she can see it

Questions every renter should ask, direct and indirect:

  • How much is the rent? / Can you tell me how much the rent is?
  • Is heat included? / Do you know if heat is included?
  • Are parking spots included? / Can you tell me whether parking spots are included?
  • How long is the lease?
  • When can I see it? / Do you know when I can see it?
  • Is there laundry in the building?
  • How much is the security deposit?

Direct questions are fast and clear on the phone. Indirect questions sound polite at a formal office. Both are correct. Use the one that fits the situation.

Guide mini-quiz

  1. Rosa wants to ask the landlord about the nearest bus stop. Which question is correct?

  2. Rosa wants to ask about the price of rent. Which question word does she use?

W17: Have to, Don't Have to, Can't

Weekly plan ·

Required lesson and practice

Have to. The landlord must fix it

Scene  East Boston Housing Hotline, January. Rosa's heat stopped working three days ago. Photo: Ketut Subiyanto / Unsplash

Lisa at the hotline answers calls like Rosa's every winter.

👩🏽
Rosa
My heat stopped working on Monday. It's freezing in my apartment. What can I do?
👩🏾
Lisa
In most apartments, the landlord has to provide heat. It's in the state sanitary code.
👩🏽
Rosa
And if he doesn't fix it?
👩🏾
Lisa
He has to fix it. You don't have to wait. You can call the health inspector. Check mass.gov for the rules.

Have to / Has to = something is required. Someone is obligated to do it. It is not a choice.

landlord's duty The landlord has to provide heat.
landlord's duty He has to fix the heater.
tenant's duty I have to pay rent by the first of the month.
tenant's duty We have to report repairs in writing.

Form: I / you / we / they have to + verb.   He / she / it has to + verb.

Choose the right sentence

Pick the correct form for each situation.

  1. The heater in Rosa's building is broken. Which sentence is correct?

    The landlord have to fix it. / The landlord has to fix it. / The landlord has to fixes it.

    Answer / teacher checkb
  2. All the tenants in Rosa's building ___ pay rent on the first. (have to / has to)

    has to / have to / having to

    Answer / teacher checkb
  3. "The landlord <strong>have to</strong> provide heat." Is this correct?

    Yes, correct. / No, should be 'has to' because landlord = he.

    Answer / teacher checkincorrect

Fill in the blank

Write the correct form: have to or has to.

  1. Lisa ___ answer the phone all day. It's her job.
    Answer / teacher checkhas to
  2. Tenants ___ report problems in writing. (Rosa's lease)
    Answer / teacher checkhave to

Unscramble the sentence

Put the words in the right order.

  1. Unscramble:
    Answer / teacher checkRosa's landlord has to repair the heater

Don't have to. You're not required

After the call, Rosa sits at her kitchen table with her lease. She checks what she has to do and what is her choice.

Rosa's lease Rule
pay rent on the 1st ✅ has to
required
tell the landlord about repairs in writing ✅ has to
required
renew in February 🔓 doesn't have to
her choice
repaint when she leaves 🔓 doesn't have to
her choice
buy a parking sticker (she has no car) 🔓 doesn't have to
not needed

Don't have to / Doesn't have to = something is NOT required. You have a choice. It is allowed, but not obligatory.

Important: Don't have to is NOT the same as can't. "You don't have to sign" = you can sign or not sign. "You can't sign" = it is not allowed.

not required Rosa doesn't have to renew.
not required Her neighbors don't have to repaint either.

    Answer / teacher check2,two

    Answer / teacher checkb

Put the words in the right order.

Fill in the blank

Write don't have to or doesn't have to.

    Answer / teacher checkdoesn't have to
  2. We ___ buy a parking sticker. We take the bus.
    Answer / teacher checkdon't have to

Can't. This is not allowed

Lisa at the hotline tells Rosa three things a landlord can't do. Rosa writes them in her notebook. These are her notes.

Rosa's notebook
What a landlord can't do
1 A landlord can't stop the heat or hot water on purpose when he has to provide it.
2 He can't punish a tenant for reporting a problem in writing.
3 He can't ask for a security deposit bigger than the first month's rent.
Rules can change. Check mass.gov for the rules.

Can't = it is not allowed. It is against the rules or the law. It is prohibited.

not allowed He can't stop the hot water on purpose.
not allowed Landlords can't punish tenants for complaining in writing.

Form: can't + base verb, with no to. He can't stop the heat. (not can't to stop)

Read Rosa's notebook

Look at Rosa's notes above. Choose the right answer.

  1. Rosa asks about a deposit. What do her notes say?

    He can't ask for more than the first month's rent. / He has to ask for two months. / He doesn't have to give it back.

    Answer / teacher checka
  2. Which sentence means it is against the rules?

    You don't have to pay a pet fee. / A landlord can't punish you for reporting a problem. / You have to sign the lease.

    Answer / teacher checkb
  3. "The landlord <strong>don't have to</strong> stop the hot water on purpose." Is this correct?

    Yes, correct. / No, should be 'can't'. Stopping it on purpose is not allowed.

    Answer / teacher checkincorrect

Fill in the blank

Write can't.

  1. A landlord ___ punish you for complaining in writing.
    Answer / teacher checkcan't
  2. He ___ turn off the hot water on purpose.
    Answer / teacher checkcan't

Putting it all together

Rosa got a tenant rights flyer at the health center. Her neighbor Diego is helping her read it on the front steps.

👨🏾
Diego
Look at this flyer. It says 'Your rights as a tenant.' Let's go through it.
👩🏽
Rosa
OK. It says owners have to heat rooms to 68 degrees or more from 7 a.m. to 11 p.m.
👨🏾
Diego
He has no choice. And this one: 'Tenants don't have to wait. They can ask the board of health to inspect.'
👩🏽
Rosa
And this: 'Landlords can't punish you for reporting a problem in writing.' Good. Then I'm calling the inspector today.
👨🏾
Diego
Good idea. Check mass.gov for the full rules too.

Quick reference

Have to / Has to = required, obligated
Don't have to / Doesn't have to = not required, your choice
Can't = not allowed, against the rules

Rules are from Massachusetts law and the state sanitary code (105 CMR 410). They can change, so check mass.gov.

Want to go deeper?: This was the quick version. If you want more examples, more exercises, and the full explanation, open the Modals: Obligation + Permission Full Guide (app reference).

Read the flyer

Each statement comes from the tenant rights flyer. Choose the best label.

  1. "The owner is required to provide heat."

    has to (required) / doesn't have to (your choice) / can't (prohibited)

    Answer / teacher checka
  2. "A deposit bigger than the first month's rent is not allowed."

    has to (required) / doesn't have to (your choice) / can't (prohibited)

    Answer / teacher checkc
  3. "Rosa is not required to renew in February."

    has to / doesn't have to / can't

    Answer / teacher checkb
  4. Diego says: "Check mass.gov for the full rules." What kind of sentence is this?

    A rule from the law: Rosa has to check mass.gov. / Good advice: it helps, but Rosa doesn't have to. / A prohibition: Rosa can't check mass.gov.

    Answer / teacher checkb

Put the words in the right order.

  1. Unscramble:
    Answer / teacher checkA landlord can't punish you for a complaint

Complete the rule

Write have to, don't have to, or can't.

  1. The landlord ___ fix a broken heater. (required)
    Answer / teacher checkhas to,have to
  2. A landlord ___ ask for a very large deposit. (not allowed)
    Answer / teacher checkcan't

Guide mini-quiz

  1. Your cousin asks if he has to come to the lease signing. He is not on the lease. Which answer is correct?

    Yes, he has to come. / No, he can't come. / No, he doesn't have to come.

    AnswerNo, he doesn't have to come.

    Doesn't have to = not required. He is allowed to come, but it is not necessary.

  2. "You don't have to pay that fee" means the same as "You can't pay that fee."

    True. Both mean you are not allowed to pay the fee. / False. Don't have to = not required. Can't = not allowed. They are different. / True. Don't have to and can't both mean the fee is optional.

    AnswerFalse. Don't have to = not required. Can't = not allowed. They are different.

    Don't have to means it is optional. Can't means it is prohibited. These are opposite ideas.

  3. Fill in the blank: "You ___ renew your lease. It is your choice." (Three words: not required.)
    Answerdon't have to

    'Don't have to' means it is not required. 'Can't' would mean it is forbidden, which is different.

  4. The sanitary code says who must provide heat. Put the words in order.
    AnswerThe owner has to provide heat

    'Has to' shows the owner is required to provide heat.

  5. Which sentence is NOT correct?

    The landlord has to provide heat. / She doesn't have to pay for normal wear. / Tenants can't to call the inspector.

    AnswerTenants can't to call the inspector.

    Can't is followed by a base verb without 'to': can't call, not can't to call.

W18: I Need to Find a Place: Infinitives

Weekly plan ·

Required lesson and practice

I Need to Move

Rosa is a hotel housekeeper. Her lease ends soon, and she needs a new apartment. Her cousin Javier comes to help her think.

Scene  Rosa's kitchen, East Boston. A Wednesday night in January. Her cousin Javier stopped by after dinner. Photo: Andres Ayrton / Unsplash
👩🏽
Rosa
My lease ends at the end of February. I need to find something fast.
👨🏿
Javier
I know. You need to call those listings tomorrow before they're gone.
👩🏽
Rosa
And I need to get the deposit together. I don't have it yet.
👨🏿
Javier
You'll need to talk to your manager about the extra shifts.

need to + base verb = something you have to do. It is necessary.

necessary I need to find a new apartment.
necessary She needs to call the landlord tomorrow.
necessary We need to move before the end of February.
The pattern:
subject + need/needs to + base verb
Base verb = no -s, no -ing, no -ed. Just the simple form.

Correct or not?

    Answer / teacher checkb

I Want to Stay Near the Bus

Bremen St. Maverick St.
💵 Rent $1,350 $1,550
🚌 Walk to bus 3 min 15 min
🛏️ Bedrooms 1 2

want to + base verb = a desire or preference. Something you would like to do.

desire I want to stay near the bus stop.
desire He wants to find a two-bedroom apartment.
negative I don't want to pay more than $1,400.
want to vs. want + noun:
I want an apartment. (noun only) I want to find an apartment. (want to + verb)

I Hope to Find Something Before Rent Goes Up

Rosa hopes to find a place before spring, when prices go up. She plans to ask every landlord about the heat. On Saturday, she reads about a teacher who also came to a new country to build a new life. Look at wanted to and needed to. They are the same pattern as want to and need to, only in the past.

Real person
Jaime Escalante, math teacher

Jaime Escalante was born in La Paz, Bolivia. In the 1960s he wanted to find a better life, so he moved to the United States. He worked many odd jobs and taught himself English. He also needed to earn another college degree before he could teach again.

In 1974 he took a job at Garfield High School in East Los Angeles. In 1982, his largest class took the AP Calculus test and passed. Some scores were questioned, and many students took the test again and passed.

Photo: Los Angeles Times, 1983, CC BY 4.0. Source: Biography.com

hope to = you want it, but you are not sure it will happen.
plan to = you have decided to do it. It is your intention.

hope I hope to find a place before rent goes up.
hope She hopes to hear back today.
plan I plan to call the landlord this afternoon.
plan They plan to move in March.

Hope to or plan to?

Choose the word that fits the meaning.

  1. Rosa is not 100% sure she will find an apartment this week. Which sentence fits?

    She plans to find one this week. / She hopes to find one this week. / She needs to find one this week.

    Answer / teacher checkb
  2. Read about Jaime Escalante. Which sentence is correct?

    He wanted moving to the United States. / He wanted to move to the United States. / He wanted to moving to the United States.

    Answer / teacher checkb
  3. How did Escalante learn English?

    He taught himself. / He learned it in Bolivia. / He learned it at Garfield High School.

    Answer / teacher checka
  4. Rosa has already decided to call the landlord at 5 PM. Which sentence fits?

    She hopes to call at 5 PM. / She plans to call at 5 PM.

    Answer / teacher checkb

Fill in the blank

Type the two words.

  1. I ___ something with laundry in the building. (hope to + find)
    Answer / teacher checkhope to find

Unscramble

Put the words in the correct order.

  1. Unscramble:
    Answer / teacher checkWe plan to move before the end of February

I Would Like to See the Apartment

The next week, Rosa has a few places to visit. She calls Brian, the landlord of the apartment on Lexington Street. This is her first call to a landlord, so she uses polite English.

Scene  East Boston. Monday after work. Rosa saw a For Rent sign on Lexington Street and now calls the number. Brian is the landlord. Photo: Scott Webb / Unsplash
🧑‍💼
Brian (landlord)
Hello, this is Brian. Can I help you?
👩🏽
Rosa
Hi. I would like to see the apartment on Lexington Street. Is it still available?
🧑‍💼
Brian (landlord)
Yes, it is. When would you like to come?
👩🏽
Rosa
I would like to come on Saturday morning, if that works.
🧑‍💼
Brian (landlord)
Saturday at 10 is fine. See you then.

would like to = a polite way to say what you want. Use it with landlords, managers, clinics, and offices.

polite I would like to see the apartment.
polite I would like to ask about the heat and hot water.
everyday I want to see the apartment. (casual, still fine)
Short form: I'd like to = I would like to. Both are correct.
On the phone or in a letter, I'd like to sounds natural and professional.

Polite or everyday?

Choose the best answer.

  1. Rosa is calling a landlord for the first time. Which sounds more appropriate?

    "I want to schedule a tour." / "I would like to schedule a tour."

    Answer / teacher checkb
  2. "She would like asking about the deposit." Is this correct?

    Correct / Not correct. Should be 'would like to ask'

    Answer / teacher checkincorrect

Fill in the blank

Type the missing words.

  1. ___ on Sunday afternoon instead. (make a polite request with 'visit')
    Answer / teacher checkI would like to visit,I'd like to visit

Unscramble

Put the words in the correct order.

  1. Unscramble:
    Answer / teacher checkI would like to ask about the deposit

Mini Review + Building the Sentence

It is Wednesday evening in early February. Rosa just got home from the hotel. Her daughter is doing homework. Rosa's lease ends in three weeks. She has talked to her cousin Javier and to Brian the landlord. Now she opens her notes app and writes everything down.

Rosa's list

  • I need to call the listing on Breed Street before 5 PM.
  • I want to find something with a second bedroom for my daughter.
  • I hope to move before the end of February.
  • I plan to ask my supervisor for Friday afternoon off so I can see apartments.
  • I would like to pay less than $1,400 a month.
All five verbs + to + base verb:
Verb Meaning Example
need to necessary I need to call now.
want to desire I want to find a bigger place.
hope to wish (unsure) I hope to move before March.
plan to intention I plan to ask for Friday afternoon off.
would like to polite want I'd like to pay less than $1,400.

Want to go deeper?: This was the quick version. For more examples, exercises, and the full explanation of gerunds vs. infinitives, open the Gerunds + Infinitives Full Guide (app reference).

Unscramble

Put the words in the correct order.

  1. Unscramble:
    Answer / teacher checkI plan to take the morning off on Friday
  2. Unscramble:
    Answer / teacher checkShe hopes to move before the end of February

Spot the error

Find what is wrong.

  1. "I would like find an apartment near the bus." What is wrong?

    Nothing is wrong. / Missing 'to'. Should be 'would like to find' / Should use 'want' instead of 'would like'

    Answer / teacher checkb
  2. Rosa is 100% sure she is calling the listing today. Which word fits best?

    She hopes to call the listing today. / She plans to call the listing today. / She would like to call the listing today.

    Answer / teacher checkb

Complete the sentence

Type the correct phrase from Rosa's list.

  1. I ___ call the listing on Breed Street before 5 PM. (need to)
    Answer / teacher checkneed to call
  2. I ___ find something with a second bedroom for my daughter. (want to)
    Answer / teacher checkwant to find

Guide mini-quiz

  1. Which sentence is correct?

    I want finding an apartment near the bus. / I want to finding an apartment near the bus. / I want to find an apartment near the bus.

    AnswerI want to find an apartment near the bus.

    After 'want', use 'to' + base verb. 'Finding' (-ing form) is not correct here.

  2. Rosa is calling a landlord for the first time. Which sounds most polite and appropriate?

    I want to look at the lease. / I would like to look at the lease. / I need to look at the lease.

    AnswerI would like to look at the lease.

    'Would like to' is more polite than 'want to'. It works better for calls with landlords, managers, and offices.

  3. Fill in the blank: "She ___ to find one before March." (She is trying but not certain she will.)
    Answerhopes

    'Hope to' means you want something but are not sure it will happen. 'Plans to' would mean she has already decided.

  4. "She needs finding a bigger apartment." What is wrong?

    Nothing is wrong. / 'finding' should be 'to find'. Use needs to + base verb. / 'bigger' should be 'more big'.

    Answer'finding' should be 'to find'. Use needs to + base verb.

    After 'need/needs', use 'to' + base verb: 'needs to find', not 'needs finding'.

  5. Rosa calls about an apartment on Lexington Street. Put the words in order.
    AnswerI would like to meet the landlord

    'Would like to' + base verb is the polite form. Use it for calls with landlords and offices.

W19: It Was Happening When: Past Tenses in Housing Stories

Weekly plan ·

Required lesson and practice

The Pipe Burst

Scene  East Boston apartment, third floor. Tuesday night, 11:45 PM. Lucia calls her landlord, Brian. Photo: Adrià Jiménez / Unsplash
👩🏽
Lucia
Brian, I'm sorry to call so late. I heard a noise from the ceiling. I looked up and saw a crack.
👨🏻
Brian
Is there any water?
👩🏽
Lucia
Yes. It came through the ceiling above the kitchen. I grabbed a bucket and I called you right away.

Past Simple = finished actions told in order. Each one happened and ended before the next one started.

finished Lucia heard a crack at midnight.
finished She saw water on the kitchen floor.
finished She called the landlord immediately.
signal words last night, right away, immediately, at midnight, then, after that

Timeline labels: heard a crack (past) → saw the water (past) → called the landlord (past)

Practice: Past Simple

Choose the correct past simple form or spot the error.

  1. Lucia ___ a noise and looked up. Which form fits?

    hears / heard / was hearing

    Answer / teacher checkheard
  2. "She <strong>grabs</strong> a bucket and called the landlord." Is this correct?

    Correct / Not correct. Should be 'grabbed' to match the past tense.

    Answer / teacher checkincorrect
  3. Unscramble to make a past simple sentence:
    Answer / teacher checkWater came through the ceiling
  4. She ___ (turn on) the light and looked around.
    Answer / teacher checkturned on

What Were You Doing?

Wednesday, 7:00 AM. Brian comes up to look at the damage and asks: "What was everyone doing?" Lucia wrote down what each person was doing the night of the leak.

Chart
Tuesday night at Lucia's apartment
11:00 11:30 11:45
🛌 Younger kids
sleep
sleep
sleep
📝 Older daughter
read
write
write
🧹 Lucia
wash
mop
mop
🍚 Rice cooker
run
run
run
💥 Pipe
· ·
burst
Look for the actions in progress. The pipe burst is the event that interrupted them.

Past Continuous = an action already in progress at a moment in the past. It was running in the background. Form: was / were + verb-ing.

in progress The kids were sleeping in the back room.
in progress The rice cooker was still running.
in progress She was mopping the floor when the water came through.

On the timeline, past continuous is a line. The pipe burst (past simple) is the dot that interrupted it.

Timeline labels: were sleeping (kids) (past) → was running (rice cooker) (past) → pipe burst (past)

Practice: Past Continuous

Choose the correct form or spot the error.

  1. Look at the chart. Which sentence is true?

    At 11:30 the younger kids were writing. / At 11:30 Lucia was mopping. / At 11:45 the younger kids were mopping.

    Answer / teacher checkb
  2. Look at the chart. Who was writing at 11:45?

    Lucia / The younger kids / The older daughter

    Answer / teacher checkdaughter
  3. "She <strong>was mop</strong> the floor when the water came through." Is this correct?

    Correct / Not correct. Should be 'was mopping'.

    Answer / teacher checkincorrect
  4. Unscramble:
    Answer / teacher checkHer daughter was reading at 11:00
  5. Look at the chart. At 11:00, Lucia ___ (wash) the dishes.
    Answer / teacher checkwas washing

When and While

Lucia's story uses when and while. So does the story of a real scientist. Read it and look for the line (in progress) and the dot (interruption).

Famous person
Katalin Karikó: A Long Road to a Nobel Prize

Katalin Karikó was born in Hungary in 1955. In 1989, she started a job at the University of Pennsylvania. She wanted to use mRNA as medicine, but it was hard to get money for her research.

She was still working on mRNA when Drew Weissman started a research group at the same university in 1997. While they were working together, they discovered a way to stop unwanted reactions to mRNA. That was in 2005. In 2023, they won the Nobel Prize.

Photo: Szeged University, 2021, CC BY-SA 4.0. Sources: Nobel Prize: Press release 2023, Nobel Prize: Katalin Karikó facts

Use when + past simple for the interruption. Use while + past continuous for the action that was in progress.

when She was mopping the floor when the pipe burst.
while While she was calling the landlord, the kids woke up.
when The kids woke up when Lucia moved the furniture.
while The rice cooker was running while everyone slept.

Quick tip: the continuous action is the background (line). The simple action is the event that cut into it or happened during it (dot).

Timeline labels: was mopping (in progress) (past) → pipe burst (interruption) (past)

Practice: When and While

Choose the correct word or form.

  1. Look at the reading. When did Karikó and Weissman make their discovery?

    1989 / 2005 / 2023

    Answer / teacher check2005
  2. Look at the reading. Which sentence about Karikó is correct?

    Weissman started his group while Karikó was living in Hungary. / Weissman started his group while Karikó was working on mRNA. / Karikó was winning the Nobel Prize when Weissman started his group.

    Answer / teacher checkb
  3. The kids woke up ___ Lucia was moving the furniture.

    when / while

    Answer / teacher checkwhile
  4. "<strong>While</strong> the pipe burst, she was mopping." Is this correct?

    Correct / Not correct. 'While' goes with the continuous action. Should be: 'While she was mopping, the pipe burst.'

    Answer / teacher checkincorrect
  5. Unscramble:
    Answer / teacher checkThe kids were sleeping when Lucia called Brian
  6. The kids ___ (sleep) while the water came through the ceiling.
    Answer / teacher checkwere sleeping

Telling the Insurance Company

Scene  Lucia's apartment. Wednesday, 11:00 AM. Her renter's insurance company calls. Photo: Vitaly Gariev / Unsplash
👩🏼
Sarah
Lucia, this is Sarah from your renter's insurance. Can you walk me through what happened?
👩🏽
Lucia
Yes. It was almost midnight. My younger kids were sleeping. I was mopping the kitchen when I heard a crack above me.
👩🏼
Sarah
And then?
👩🏽
Lucia
Water came down fast. I grabbed a bucket. While I was holding the bucket, I called the landlord with my other hand.
👩🏼
Sarah
Okay, I have enough to file the claim. Thank you.

Lucia uses both tenses together: past simple for the sequence of events, past continuous for what was already happening in the background. Choose the right tense for each blank below.

Practice: Choose the Right Tense

Choose past simple or past continuous based on meaning.

  1. The kids ___ when the pipe burst. (They were already in bed.)

    slept (past simple) / were sleeping (past continuous)

    Answer / teacher checkwere sleeping
  2. Lucia ___ a bucket right away. (One quick action.)

    grabbed (past simple) / was grabbing (past continuous)

    Answer / teacher checkgrabbed
  3. While she ___ the bucket, she called the landlord.

    held (past simple) / was holding (past continuous)

    Answer / teacher checkwas holding
  4. "Sarah called Lucia while she was cleaning up the water." Which action was already in progress?

    Sarah calling / Lucia cleaning up / Both were in progress.

    Answer / teacher checkb
  5. Water ___ (come) down fast when Lucia grabbed a bucket.
    Answer / teacher checkcame

Find the mistakes
Lucia's first draft (some sentences are wrong)

Read each sentence. Is the tense right for the meaning?

Help Lucia fix her statement for the inspector's report.

Want to go deeper?: This was the quick version. If you want more examples, more exercises, and the full explanation, open the Past Simple + Past Continuous Full Guide (app reference).

Practice: Error Correction

Find the error in each sentence from Lucia's statement.

  1. Look at the statement. Which sentences have a mistake?

    Sentence 1 only / Sentences 1 and 3 / Sentences 2 and 3

    Answer / teacher checkb
  2. Sentence 1: "The kids were sleep in the back room when the pipe burst."

    Correct / Not correct. Should be 'were sleeping' (was/were + verb-ing).

    Answer / teacher checkincorrect
  3. Sentence 2: "I was mopping the kitchen when I heard a crack."

    Correct / Not correct.

    Answer / teacher checkcorrect
  4. Sentence 3: "While the water came down, I was grabbing a bucket and called the landlord."

Guide mini-quiz

  1. Which sentence is correct?

    The kids were sleep when the pipe burst. / The kids was sleeping when the pipe burst. / The kids were sleeping when the pipe burst.

    AnswerThe kids were sleeping when the pipe burst.

    Past continuous with a plural subject = were + verb-ing. 'Were sleep' and 'was sleeping' are both incorrect forms.

  2. Lucia was mopping the floor when the pipe burst. Which action was already in progress?

    The pipe bursting / Lucia mopping / Both were already in progress.

    AnswerLucia mopping

    Past continuous (was mopping) shows the background action in progress. Past simple (burst) is the event that interrupted it.

  3. Fill in the blank: "While Lucia ___ the landlord, the kids woke up." (Action in progress: past continuous.)
    Answerwas calling

    'While' introduces the action that was in progress, so past continuous (was calling) is needed. 'Called' would use past simple.

  4. Which sentence has an error?

    She was holding the bucket when she called him. / Water came through the ceiling at midnight. / The rice cooker were running all night.

    AnswerThe rice cooker were running all night.

    'The rice cooker' is singular, so the correct form is 'was running,' not 'were running.'

  5. Lucia was cleaning the kitchen when the pipe burst. Put the words in order.
    AnswerShe was mopping when it burst

    Past continuous (was mopping) = the background action. Past simple (burst) = the event that interrupted it.

Week 19 Quiz · required
  1. hear → V1-s (he/she/it)
    Answerhears

    V1-s (he/she/it) of hear: hears.

  2. hear → V-ing
    Answerhearing

    V-ing of hear: hearing.

  3. hear → V2 (past)
    Answerheard

    V2 (past) of hear: heard.

  4. hear → V3 (past participle)
    Answerheard

    V3 (past participle) of hear: heard.

  5. leave → V1-s (he/she/it)
    Answerleaves

    V1-s (he/she/it) of leave: leaves.

  6. leave → V-ing
    Answerleaving

    V-ing of leave: leaving.

  7. leave → V2 (past)
    Answerleft

    V2 (past) of leave: left.

  8. leave → V3 (past participle)
    Answerleft

    V3 (past participle) of leave: left.

  9. I was cooking when I ___ a loud noise. (hear)
    Answerheard

    I was cooking when I heard a loud noise. (hear)

  10. While I was locking the door, my neighbor ___ the building. (leave)
    Answerleft

    While I was locking the door, my neighbor left the building. (leave)

  11. Which word means “to stop something bad from happening”?

    prevent / fix / maintain

    prevent: to stop something bad from happening. Regular cleaning can prevent mold in the bathroom.

  12. Which word means “to return money someone spent or lent”?

    fix / maintain / pay back

    Answerpay back

    pay back: to return money someone spent or lent. Will the landlord pay back the money I spent on the repair?

  13. Lucia was mopping the floor when the pipe burst. Which action was already in progress?

    The pipe bursting / Lucia mopping / Both were already in progress.

    AnswerLucia mopping

    Past continuous (was mopping) shows the background action in progress. Past simple (burst) is the event that interrupted it.

  14. Fill in the blank: "While Lucia ___ the landlord, the kids woke up." (Action in progress: past continuous.)
    Answerwas calling

    'While' introduces the action that was in progress, so past continuous (was calling) is needed. 'Called' would use past simple.

W20: Past Perfect: What Had Already Happened

Weekly plan ·

Required lesson and practice

She Had Already Done the Work

Scene  East Boston. A warehouse off Chelsea Street. Wednesday morning. Photo: Ruchindra Gunasekara / Unsplash
👩🏽
Gloria
I'm nervous. I've never applied to a warehouse before.
🧑🏻
Receptionist
Don't worry. The manager said you already have good experience.
👩🏽
Gloria
That’s true. Before I applied, I had worked in housekeeping for two years. I just hope that’s enough.

Past Perfect = something that finished before another past moment. Use it to show which action happened first when telling a story about the past.

1st action She had worked in housekeeping for two years.
2nd action She applied for the warehouse job.
together By the time she applied, she had already worked two years in housekeeping.

The first action (working in housekeeping) uses had + past participle. The second action (applied) uses Past Simple. You almost always need both verbs to make the sequence clear.

Timeline labels: Past Perfect (1st) (past-earlier) → Past Simple (2nd) (past-later)

Which happened first?

Read each sentence. Which action happened first?

  1. By the time Gloria walked in, the manager had already called her references.

    She walked into the warehouse / The manager called her references

    Answer / teacher checkb
  2. When the manager called her, she had already sent her application.

    She sent her application / The manager called her

    Answer / teacher checka

Complete the sentence

Fill in the blank with the correct Past Perfect form (had + past participle).

  1. By the time she got the interview, she ___ (work) at the hotel for two years.
    Answer / teacher checkhad worked
  2. When the manager came out, Gloria ___ (already arrive) at the front desk.
    Answer / teacher checkhad already arrived

had + V3: Putting It in Order

It is Wednesday morning in East Boston. Gloria sits in the warehouse break room before her interview and checks her list. A green check means she had done it before today.

Before the interview
Gloria's application checklist
✅ Gloria had cleaned hotel rooms for two years.
✅ She had handled supply orders at the hotel.
✅ She had sent her application online.
⬜ She hadn't driven a forklift.
⬜ She hadn't worked in a warehouse.

Positive: subject + had + past participle
Negative: subject + hadn't + past participle
Every person uses had. There is no "hads" or "has had."

positive She had cleaned hotel rooms for two years before she applied here.
negative Gloria hadn't driven a forklift before the training.
negative They hadn't finished loading the truck when the manager arrived.
Common irregular past participles to know:
go → gone see → seen do → done take → taken have → had leave → left work → worked save → saved

Correct or not correct?

Is the Past Perfect form correct?

  1. "Before the shift, she had ate her lunch."

    Correct / Not correct. Should be: had eaten

    Answer / teacher checkincorrect
  2. "He hadn't worked in a warehouse before this job."

    Correct / Not correct

    Answer / teacher checkcorrect
  3. Look at Gloria's checklist. Which sentence is true?

    Before the interview, she had sent her application, but she hadn't worked in a warehouse. / Before the interview, she hadn't sent her application. / Before the interview, she had driven a forklift.

    Answer / teacher checka

Build the sentence

Fill in the blank with the correct form: positive (had + V3) or negative (hadn't + V3).

  1. Before the safety training, Gloria ___ (never use) a pallet jack.
    Answer / teacher checkhad never used,hadn't used
  2. Before the interview, Gloria ___ (send) her application online.
    Answer / teacher checkhad sent

Put the words in order

Unscramble the words to make a correct sentence.

  1. Unscramble:
    Answer / teacher checkShe had saved enough before she applied

When, Before, After, By the Time

Scene  HR office. Jennifer, the hiring manager, interviews Gloria. Photo: Amy Hirschi / Unsplash
👩‍💼
Jennifer
Had you ever done inventory work before you applied here?
👩🏽
Gloria
Yes. After I had finished my shift at the hotel, I helped count stock.
👩‍💼
Jennifer
And by the time you left that job, had you trained anyone?
👩🏽
Gloria
I had trained two new cleaners before I left.
👩‍💼
Jennifer
That's great experience. We'd like to offer you the job. Can you start Monday?

Four words help you show which action came first. Learn them and you can use Past Perfect naturally.

when

When she arrived, the manager had already called her references.
When + Past Simple shows the second action. Past Perfect shows what finished first.

before

She had trained two people before she left.
Past Perfect + before + Past Simple.

after

After she had finished her shift, she helped count stock.
After + Past Perfect, Past Simple.

by the time

By the time she applied, she had worked there for two years.
By the time + Past Simple, Past Perfect for the earlier action.

Choose the correct signal word

Pick the word that fits the sentence naturally.

  1. ___ the interviewer asked about her references, Gloria had already sent them.

    By the time / After

    Answer / teacher checka
  2. ___ she had finished the paperwork, Jennifer shook her hand.

    After / By the time

    Answer / teacher checka

Complete the sentence

Fill in the blank with the correct Past Perfect form.

  1. When Jennifer asked for her references, Gloria ___ (already send) them by email.
    Answer / teacher checkhad already sent
  2. Before she walked into the interview, she ___ (practice) her answers with a friend.
    Answer / teacher checkhad practiced

Put the words in order

Unscramble to make a correct sentence.

  1. Unscramble:
    Answer / teacher checkBy the time she left the hotel she had trained two people

Past Perfect vs. Past Simple

Marta used to clean rooms with Gloria at the hotel. She still works there. Gloria calls her on Wednesday evening with the good news. Here is Gloria's day.

Wednesday
Gloria's big day
8:00 AM
Gloria arrived at the warehouse.
9:00 AM
The interview started.
10:00 AM
Jennifer offered her the job.
6:00 PM
Gloria called Marta.

Use Past Simple for one finished action in the past.
Use Past Perfect only when you have two past actions and need to show which one came first.

one action Jennifer offered her the job today. (just one past fact)
two actions Before she got the job, she had trained two new cleaners. (1st: trained; 2nd: got the job)
two actions When Gloria called Marta, Jennifer had already offered her the job. (1st: offered; 2nd: called)

Common mistake: Using Past Perfect for a single action.
✗ "I had worked yesterday." (only one action, no sequence)
✓ "I worked yesterday."

Timeline labels: Past Simple (alone) (past) → Past Perfect (1st) (past-earlier) → Past Simple (2nd) (past-later)

One action or two?

Choose Past Simple or Past Perfect based on whether there is one action or a sequence.

  1. Gloria ___ the warehouse job today. (one fact, no sequence)

    got (Past Simple) / had got (Past Perfect)

    Answer / teacher checka
  2. Before she applied here, Gloria ___ every shift on time at the hotel.

    showed up (Past Simple) / had shown up (Past Perfect)

    Answer / teacher checkb
  3. Look at the timeline. When Gloria called Marta, Jennifer ___ her the job.

    offered (Past Simple) / had already offered (Past Perfect)

    Answer / teacher checkb

Error check

Which sentence has a mistake?

  1. Which sentence is NOT correct?

    She had worked a double shift before she got the job. / She had finished her break yesterday. / By the time the manager arrived, they had loaded the truck.

    Answer / teacher checkb

Fill in the correct tense

Write the correct form of the verb. Use Past Simple or Past Perfect.

  1. Gloria ___ (work) at the hotel for two years before she got the warehouse job.
    Answer / teacher checkhad worked
  2. She ___ (call) Marta right after Jennifer offered her the job.
    Answer / teacher checkcalled
  3. Look at the timeline. By the time the interview started, Gloria ___ (arrive) at the warehouse.
    Answer / teacher checkhad arrived

Your Work Story

Work histories use Past Perfect all the time. Gloria reads about a woman who had worked very hard jobs before she started a business. Look for the two actions in each sentence.

A real work story
Madam C. J. Walker

Sarah Breedlove was born in Louisiana in 1867. She lost her parents when she was seven. Before she started her own business, she had worked as a farm laborer and a laundress.

In the 1890s, she lost much of her hair because of a scalp problem. In 1905, she moved to Denver. There, she began her own business as “Madam” C. J. Walker. Before she settled in Indianapolis in 1910, she had traveled through the South and Southeast, selling door to door. In Indianapolis, she built a factory and a training school.

Photo: Addison N. Scurlock, c. 1914, public domain. Source: Madam C. J. Walker official site

Past Perfect is natural in work histories: you talk about what you had done before the current job, and what had already happened before a key moment.

experience Before this job, I had worked in a hotel for three years.
never before I had never driven a forklift before they trained me here.
already done By the time I applied, I had already saved for three months.

Tell your own work story: Before her interview, Gloria had never told her work history in English. Practice yours: say what you had done before your last job, and what you had never done.

Madam C. J. Walker's story

Look at the reading about Madam C. J. Walker.

  1. Which happened first?

    Walker settled in Indianapolis / Walker traveled through the South and Southeast

    Answer / teacher checkb
  2. Walker ___ (be) a laundress before she started her own business.
    Answer / teacher checkhad been
  3. By the time Walker settled in Indianapolis, she ___ (already begin) her business in Denver.
    Answer / teacher checkhad already begun

Gloria's story

Choose the correct form.

  1. Before Gloria started at the warehouse, she ___ a forklift.

    had never driven / has never driven

    Answer / teacher checka

Your work history

Put the words in the right order.

  1. Unscramble:
    Answer / teacher checkBefore I came here I had never worked nights

Guide mini-quiz

  1. By the time Gloria walked into the warehouse, she ___ two years in housekeeping.

    has worked / had worked / worked

    Answerhad worked

    Past Perfect (had worked) shows the earlier action that finished before she walked in.

  2. Gloria hadn't driven a forklift before she ___.

    starts at this warehouse / started at this warehouse / had started at this warehouse

    Answerstarted at this warehouse

    The second action uses Past Simple. Only the first (earlier) action uses Past Perfect.

  3. Fill in the blank: "Before Gloria got the job, she ___ hotel rooms for two years." (Earlier of two past actions.)
    Answerhad cleaned

    Past Perfect (had cleaned) shows the action that happened first, before she got the new job.

  4. Which sentence has a mistake?

    After she had finished loading, she clocked out. / She had eaten lunch before the break ended. / I had called Marta last night.

    AnswerI had called Marta last night.

    Past Perfect needs two past actions. 'Last night' is just one action, so Past Simple (called) is correct.

  5. Gloria finished her tasks before the manager arrived. Put the words in order.
    AnswerShe had finished before the manager arrived

    Past Perfect (had finished) = the earlier action. Past Simple (arrived) = the later action.

Week 20 Quiz · required
  1. become → V1-s (he/she/it)
    Answerbecomes

    V1-s (he/she/it) of become: becomes.

  2. become → V-ing
    Answerbecoming

    V-ing of become: becoming.

  3. become → V2 (past)
    Answerbecame

    V2 (past) of become: became.

  4. become → V3 (past participle)
    Answerbecome

    V3 (past participle) of become: become.

  5. lead → V1-s (he/she/it)
    Answerleads

    V1-s (he/she/it) of lead: leads.

  6. lead → V-ing
    Answerleading

    V-ing of lead: leading.

  7. lead → V2 (past)
    Answerled

    V2 (past) of lead: led.

  8. lead → V3 (past participle)
    Answerled

    V3 (past participle) of lead: led.

  9. go → V1-s (he/she/it)
    Answergoes

    V1-s (he/she/it) of go: goes.

  10. go → V-ing
    Answergoing

    V-ing of go: going.

  11. go → V2 (past)
    Answerwent

    V2 (past) of go: went.

  12. go → V3 (past participle)
    Answergone

    V3 (past participle) of go: gone.

  13. Before I applied, I had ___ a team leader. (become)
    Answerbecome

  14. She had ___ two projects before her promotion. (lead)

  15. Check the _____ to see which days you work next week.

  16. Which word means “a short rest from work”?

    Answerbreak

  17. When the manager arrived, I had already finished my tasks. What happened first?

  18. Gloria finished her tasks before the manager arrived. Put the words in order. Words: She / had / finished / before / the / manager / arrived
    AnswerShe had finished before the manager arrived

    Past Perfect (had finished) = the earlier action. Past Simple (arrived) = the later action.

W21: I Used to, but Now I...

Weekly plan ·

Required lesson and practice

Life Was Different Back Home

Bring back: Workplace warm-up: You have to wear closed-toe shoes. You should arrive a little early. You cannot block the exit. Then compare: I used to work nights; now I work days.

Scene  On the bus to work. Tuesday, 4:30 AM. Photo: Jivan Garcha / Unsplash

Linh works as a housekeeper at a hotel in East Boston. She moved from Vietnam four years ago. Her shift is 5 AM to 1 PM. On the bus to work, she video-calls her sister Mai. It is afternoon in Vietnam.

👩🏻
Mai
How are the kids?
👩🏻
Linh
They're good. Busy with school.
👩🏻
Linh
They miss you. I used to have family nearby to help. Now we only see you on the phone.
👩🏻
Mai
I know. It's hard.

Used to + base verb = a past habit or state that is not true now. It is not the same as am used to (introduced in Week 33).

past habit I used to have family nearby. (Not true now.)
formula Subject + used to + base verb (no -ing, no -ed on the main verb)

Timeline labels: used to + verb (old habit) (past) → now (changed) (present)

What does used to mean?

Choose the best answer.

  1. "I used to have family nearby." What is true now?

    Linh still has family nearby. / Linh does not have family nearby anymore. / Linh will have family nearby in the future.

    Answer / teacher checkb

Fill in the blank

Write the missing word.

  1. I ___ to have family nearby.
    Answer / teacher checkused

Unscramble

  1. Build Linh's sentence about her old neighborhood:
    Answer / teacher checkI used to know all my neighbors

I Didn't Use To...

Linh's coworker Michelle asks how her days changed after she moved to Boston. Linh writes it down for her.

Then and now
Linh's day: Vietnam and Boston
Back home Boston now
Wake up 6:30 4:00
Work starts 8:00 5:00
Dinner cook at 11 pm meal-prep on Sunday

Negative: didn't use to + base verb. No -d on use.
Question: Did you use to + base verb?

negative I didn't use to wake up at 4. (Now I do.)
question Did you use to work night shifts?

Choose the correct negative

Pick the correct form.

  1. Look at the table. What time did Linh use to wake up back home?

    4:00 / 6:30 / 8:00

    Answer / teacher checkb
  2. Michelle asks about Linh's old schedule. Which question is correct?
