W29: Stop Taking It or Stop to Take It?

Weekly plan ·

Required lesson and practice

Stop Taking the Old Medicine

Bring back W23: I enjoy walking. I want to walk. Today we compare patterns that change the meaning.

Scene  East Boston Pharmacy on Meridian Street, Thursday 10:15 PM. Photo: Unsplash / Unsplash

Marisol just finished her closing shift at the warehouse. She stops at the pharmacy on the way home. The pharmacist, Jennifer, has her new prescription ready, but there's something important she needs to know.

👩🏾
Jennifer
Marisol, the doctor changed your prescription. You need to stop taking the old blood pressure pills tonight.
👩🏽
Marisol
Stop taking them? Even if I still have some at home?
👩🏾
Jennifer
Yes. Stop taking them completely. Don't mix the two medications.

Here, stop taking refers to Marisol’s old pills. That means: she was taking the pills before, and now she needs to end that habit.

stop + -ing = end an ongoing action. You were doing it. Now you stop.

She stopped taking the old pills.  → She was taking them. Now she stopped.

stop + -ing Stop taking the white pills. (You were taking them. End it.)
stop + -ing She stopped smoking last year. (She smoked. She quit.)
stop + -ing He stopped working at midnight. (He was working. Then he stopped.)

What does it mean?

Choose the meaning of each sentence.

  1. "She stopped taking the old pills."

    She was taking the pills before, and now she has ended that. / She paused her other activity to take the pills. / She is going to take the pills later.

    Answer / teacher checka
  2. "He stopped working at the warehouse."

    He went to the warehouse in order to work. / He was working there, and now he is not. / He will start working at the warehouse.

    Answer / teacher checkb

Fill in the blank

Write the correct -ing form of the verb in parentheses.

  1. The pharmacist said: "Stop ___ (take) the white pills immediately."
    Answer / teacher checktaking

Unscramble

  1. Unscramble:
    Answer / teacher checkShe stopped taking the old medication last Thursday

Stop to Take It With Food

Scene  Break room at the warehouse, Friday lunchtime. Photo: Centre for Ageing Better / Unsplash

The next day at work, Kevin checks whether Marisol is ready to return from break. She explains why she paused and clears up a misunderstanding about her new prescription.

👨🏻
Kevin
Are you coming back to the floor? Our break is nearly over.
👩🏽
Marisol
In a minute. I stopped to take my new pill. The label says to take it with food.
👨🏻
Kevin
Oh, I thought the doctor told you to stop taking your pills.
👩🏽
Marisol
Just the old ones. I stopped taking those yesterday. This is the new prescription.

Kevin learns why Marisol paused. Stop + to + verb means you pause your current activity in order to do a new one. Two different actions.

stop + to + verb = pause what you're doing in order to do something else. Two actions.

She stopped to take her pill.  → She was doing something. She paused. She took the pill.

stop + to She stopped working to take her pill. (She paused work, then took the pill.)
stop + to He stopped at the pharmacy to pick up the prescription.
contrast Stop taking it = end the habit.   Stop to take it = pause and do it now.

Which meaning?

Choose the correct meaning.

  1. "Marisol stopped to take her pill at noon."

    Marisol ended the habit of taking the pill. / Marisol paused what she was doing in order to take the pill. / Marisol forgot to take the pill.

    Answer / teacher checkb
  2. "Kevin stopped eating to answer his phone."

    Kevin quit eating forever. / Kevin paused his meal to answer the phone. / Kevin ate and answered the phone at the same time.

    Answer / teacher checkb

Stop taking or stop to take?

Choose the correct form for each sentence.

  1. The doctor told her to ___ the old medication. (end the habit)

    stop taking / stop to take

    Answer / teacher checkstop taking
  2. She ___ her lunch ___ her pill. (she paused eating, then took the pill)

    stopped eating / to take / stopped eating / taking

    Answer / teacher checkstopped eating / to take

Fill in the blank

Write 'taking' or 'to take'.

  1. At noon, Marisol stopped ___ her pill with her sandwich. (She paused her work.)
    Answer / teacher checkto take

Try Taking the Generic / Try to Get Covered

It's Friday evening. Marisol gets a text from the East Boston Pharmacy. It explains why her new bottle says "generic." Look at the three steps.

Text message
East Boston Pharmacy: your refill
1 Your generic refill is ready. Try taking it at the same time every day.
2 Your insurance does not cover the name brand. You can try to get it covered. Ask your doctor's office about a prior authorization.
3 Their phone line is busy on Mondays. Try to call before 10 AM.
Questions about your medicine? Ask your pharmacist or doctor.

Notice the two uses: try taking (an experiment, easy to do) and try to get / try to call (an effort, it may be difficult and may not work).

try + -ing = experiment with something to see if it works. Low effort, worth trying.

try + to + verb = make an effort to do something. It may be difficult. You might not succeed.

try + -ing Try taking your pill at the same time every day. (experiment)
try + to She tried to get the name brand covered, but the insurance said no. (effort, difficult)
try + -ing Try walking to the bus stop. (experiment, you might like it)
try + to Try to get eight hours of sleep. (a goal, may be hard)

Read the text message

Look at the pharmacy text. Choose the best answer.

  1. Which step asks Marisol to experiment with something easy?

    Step 1 / Step 2 / Step 3

    Answer / teacher check1
  2. Step 2 is about the name brand. What kind of action is it?

    An experiment: easy, just see what happens / An effort: it may be hard and may not work

    Answer / teacher checkeffort
  3. Which sentence is a good report of Step 3?

    The pharmacy told her to try calling Mondays. / The pharmacy told her to try to call early. / The pharmacy told her to stop to call.

    Answer / teacher checkb

Choose the correct form

  1. The pharmacist said, "___ the generic. It is the same medicine." (suggestion to experiment)

    Try taking / Try to take

    Answer / teacher checkTry taking
  2. She ___ fix the insurance mistake, but the call dropped three times. (difficult effort)

    tried fixing / tried to fix

    Answer / teacher checktried to fix

Fill in the blank

Write 'taking' or 'to take'.

  1. I tried ___ the generic pill for a month, and it worked fine. (I experimented, use -ing form)
    Answer / teacher checktaking

Unscramble

  1. Unscramble:
    Answer / teacher checkShe tried to get the prescription covered by insurance

Remember to Take It / I Remember Taking It

Saturday morning, 8:30 AM. Marisol checks her list. Some things are done. Some things are still ahead.

Marisol's Saturday
Done and not done yet
✅ I remember taking my pill at 7:00 with breakfast.
✅ I remember setting the alarm last night.
⬜ Remember to take the pill before the early shift tomorrow.
⬜ Remember to call the clinic on Monday.

Two uses, two meanings. Remember taking it means she's looking back at something she already did (✅). Remember to take it means she's looking forward at something she must not forget (⬜).

remember + to + verb = don't forget to do it (future / task). Looking forward.

remember + -ing = you recall doing it (past / memory). Looking back.

future task Remember to take your pill before breakfast. (Don't forget, task ahead.)
past memory I remember taking it at seven. (I recall it, it already happened.)
future task Remember to call the clinic on Monday. (Task, don't forget.)
past memory Do you remember filling out the form last week? (Memory, did you do it?)

Read the checklist

Look at Marisol's Saturday list.

  1. Which thing does Marisol still need to do?

    Set the alarm / Call the clinic / Eat breakfast with her pill

    Answer / teacher checkb
  2. The checked items (✅) use which pattern?

    remember + -ing (past memory) / remember + to (future task)

    Answer / teacher checkgerund

Future task or past memory?

Decide what each sentence means.

  1. "Remember to pick up your prescription on Thursday."

    Future task, don't forget to do this / Past memory, recalling something that happened

    Answer / teacher checkfuture
  2. "I remember taking the last pill on Sunday morning."

    Future task, a reminder for later / Past memory, recalling something already done

    Answer / teacher checkpast
  3. Don't forget, ___ your pill before the shift. (looking forward: task)

    remember taking / remember to take

    Answer / teacher checkremember to take

Fill in the blank

Write the correct form.

  1. The doctor's note says: Remember ___ the pill every morning with food. (future task)
    Answer / teacher checkto take

Unscramble

  1. Unscramble:
    Answer / teacher checkI remember locking the locker before I left for work

Stop Taking vs Stop to Take

Jennifer, the pharmacist, gives Marisol one last tip: the two stop patterns look almost the same, but the meaning is very different. Compare them side by side.

Compare
stop + -ing or stop + to?
stop + -ing stop + to
End it.
You do it no more.		 Pause.
Then do something new.
She stopped smoking last year. She stopped to buy water.
Marisol stopped taking the old pills. Marisol stopped to take a pill at noon.
Kevin stopped working at the warehouse. Kevin stopped working to answer his phone.
Left: the habit is over. Right: one short stop, then the first activity may continue.

Quick reference:

stop + -ing = end an ongoing action

stop + to = pause to do something else

try + -ing = experiment, see if it works

try + to = make an effort (may be difficult)

remember + to = don't forget (future task)

remember + -ing = recall a past action (memory)

Use the table

Look at the comparison table.

  1. In which column does the habit end completely?

    The stop + -ing column / The stop + to column

    Answer / teacher checking
  2. "Kevin stopped working to answer his phone." What happened?

    Kevin lost his job. / Kevin paused work for a moment to use the phone. / Kevin will answer the phone tomorrow.

    Answer / teacher checkb

Match the meaning

Choose the sentence that matches what the label means.

  1. A label says: 'Stop taking this medicine and call your doctor.' This means:

    Pause and take the medicine now. / End the habit. If you are not sure, ask your pharmacist or doctor. / Experiment with the medicine to see if it works.

    Answer / teacher checkb
  2. A tip says: 'Try taking your pill with breakfast.' This means:

    It's very hard to take this pill. / Experiment: do it at breakfast and see if it is easier. / You must take it at breakfast or it won't work.

    Answer / teacher checkb

Spot the error

One sentence has a grammar mistake. Find it.

  1. "Marisol stopped to take the old pills last week." (She ended that habit)

    Correct / Not correct. Should be 'stopped taking'. She ended the habit, not paused to do it.

    Answer / teacher checkincorrect
  2. "I tried to get the refill on Friday, but the pharmacy was closed." (She made an effort)

    Correct. She made an effort, so 'tried to get' fits. / Not correct, must use 'tried getting'

    Answer / teacher checkcorrect

Fill in the blank

Write the correct form: -ing or to + verb.

  1. I remember ___ (fill out) the form at the clinic last week. I can picture the pen. (past memory, use -ing)
    Answer / teacher checkfilling out

Unscramble

  1. Unscramble:
    Answer / teacher checkRemember to pick up the refill before your shift ends

Guide mini-quiz

  1. The pharmacist says: 'You need to stop ___ the old blood pressure pills.' Which word fits?

    to take / taking / take

    Answertaking

    'Stop taking' means end an ongoing habit. She was taking the pills before, and now she needs to stop.

  2. Marisol was working on the warehouse floor. At noon, she stopped ___ her pill. (She paused her work to take the pill.)

    to take / taking / took

    Answerto take

    'Stop to take' means pause your current activity in order to do something else. Two different actions.

  3. Fill in the blank: "Jennifer asks: 'Did you take your pill this morning?' Marisol says: 'Yes, I remember ___ it at 7 AM.'" (She is recalling a past memory.)
    Answertaking

    'Remember taking' = recalling a past event. Something that already happened.

  4. Which sentence has an error?

    She stopped smoking last year. / She stopped to smoke last year. (meaning: she quit the habit) / She stopped to read the label before taking the pill.

    AnswerShe stopped to smoke last year. (meaning: she quit the habit)

    To describe quitting a habit, use 'stop + -ing': stopped smoking. 'Stopped to smoke' means she paused to smoke. That's the opposite meaning.

  5. Marisol's doctor told her to change an evening habit. Put the words in order.
    AnswerShe stopped drinking coffee at night

    'Stopped drinking' means she ended the habit of drinking coffee at night.

W30: The Doctor Said: Reported Speech

Weekly plan ·

Required lesson and practice

The Clinic Call

Bring back: Core practice: She said that she needed rest (statement). She told me to rest (instruction). Try one of each, then use the remaining class block for catch-up work.

Scene  East Boston Neighborhood Health Center. Tuesday, 4:30 PM. Photo: Towfiqu barbhuiya / Unsplash

Luz is at home with her daughter Amina, who has asthma. Marco is still at the restaurant finishing his line-cook shift. The clinic calls about Amina's inhaler.

👩‍⚕️
Nurse Kelly
Hi, this is Kelly from East Boston Neighborhood Health Center. Our records show Amina's blue inhaler is almost empty.
👩🏿
Luz
Yes, hi. She used it twice last night.
👩‍⚕️
Nurse Kelly
The doctor says the pharmacy can refill it today if you come before 6.
👩🏿
Luz
OK. I'll write it down and tell my husband.

Reported speech means you tell someone else what another person said. You are not repeating the exact words. You change the form: present becomes past, can becomes could, will becomes would.

Direct: Kelly says, "The pharmacy can refill it." exact words
Reported: Kelly said that the pharmacy could refill it. reported

Luz needs to tell Marco everything. She won't use Kelly's exact words. She will report what Kelly said.

Timeline labels: what they said (past) → you report it (present)

Direct or Reported?

Choose the reported speech sentence.

  1. Kelly spoke to Luz on the phone. Which sentence is reported speech?

    Kelly said, "The pharmacy can refill it today." / Kelly said that the pharmacy could refill it today. / Can the pharmacy refill it today?

    Answer / teacher checkb

Fill in the Blank

Write the reporting verb.

  1. Luz tells Marco: "Kelly ___ that Amina's inhaler was almost empty."
    Answer / teacher checksaid

Unscramble

  1. Unscramble this reported sentence:
    Answer / teacher checkKelly said that the clinic called about the inhaler

Telling Marco: She Said That…

People report famous words all the time. Read what Lupita Nyong'o said when she won an Oscar. Then see how Luz uses the same pattern in a text to Marco.

Famous person
Lupita Nyong'o: Her Oscar Speech

Lupita Nyong'o was born in Mexico and grew up in Kenya. She came to the United States to study, and she graduated from the Yale School of Drama in 2012. On March 2, 2014, she won an Oscar for the film 12 Years a Slave.

In her speech, she said that she wanted to thank her family and her drama school for their training. She told her brother that he was her best friend. At the end, she said that no matter where children were from, their dreams were valid.

Photo: Gage Skidmore, 2016, CC BY-SA 3.0. Sources: Academy Awards Acceptance Speeches Database, Yale: Lupita Nyong'o

When you report a statement, the verb often moves back one step: is → was, can → could, will → would. Use said that + subject + verb.

is → was Direct: "You are my best friend." → Reported: She told him he was her best friend.
can → could Direct: "We can refill it." → Reported: She said they could refill it.
will → would Direct: "The doctor will call tomorrow." → Reported: She said the doctor would call tomorrow.

Back at the clinic call, Luz uses this pattern. Marco is wiping down the prep station at the restaurant when she texts him: "Kelly said that we could get the inhaler refilled today." A little later: "She said that we had to get there before 6."

Timeline labels: direct (is, can, will) (present) → reported (was, could, would) (past)

Change to Reported Speech

Choose the correct reported sentence.

  1. Lupita Nyong'o said: "No matter where you're from, your dreams are valid." How do you report this?

    She said that no matter where children were from, their dreams were valid. / She said that no matter where children from, their dreams valid. / She said that were their dreams valid no matter where children were from.

    Answer / teacher checka
  2. Kelly said: "The pharmacy closes at 6." How does Luz report this?

    Kelly said that the pharmacy closing at 6. / Kelly said that the pharmacy closed at 6. / Kelly said that does the pharmacy close at 6.

    Answer / teacher checkb

Read the Card

Look at the reading about Lupita Nyong'o.

  1. Which sentence is true?

    Lupita grew up in Mexico. / Lupita grew up in Kenya. / Lupita grew up in the United States.

    Answer / teacher checkb
  2. In what year did Lupita graduate from the Yale School of Drama? Write the year.
    Answer / teacher check2012

Fill in the Blank

Write the back-shifted verb.

  1. Direct: "The doctor will call tomorrow." Reported: Luz said the doctor ___ call tomorrow.
    Answer / teacher checkwould

Unscramble

  1. Unscramble:
    Answer / teacher checkShe said that the pharmacy could refill it today

He Told Me To…

Wednesday morning. Marco picked up the new inhaler before 6, and the pharmacist gave him this sheet. Their cousin Gloria is watching Amina before school, so Marco tells her what the pharmacist said.

Pharmacy sheet
Amina's inhaler
1 Shake the inhaler before each use.
2 Keep it at room temperature. Don't leave it in a cold car.
3 Don't use the old inhaler. It is expired.
4 Call the clinic if her breathing gets worse.
Marco reads this sheet to Gloria. He says: "The pharmacist told me to..."

For commands and advice, use told / asked + person + to + verb. For negative commands: told + person + not to + verb.

told me to Direct: "Keep it at room temperature." → He told me to keep it at room temperature.
asked me to Direct: "Please call if symptoms get worse." → He asked me to call if symptoms got worse.
told me not to Direct: "Don't leave it in a cold car." → He told us not to leave it in a cold car.

Tonight Marco will call his mother Lucia in Guatemala. She worries about Amina, so he will tell her what the clinic and the pharmacist said.

Choose the Reported Command

Pick the correct reported form.

  1. The pharmacist said: "Shake the inhaler before each use." How does Marco report this?

    The pharmacist told me shaking the inhaler before each use. / The pharmacist told me to shake the inhaler before each use. / The pharmacist told me shake the inhaler before each use.

    Answer / teacher checkb
  2. Look at the pharmacy sheet. Which sentence is true?

    The pharmacist told us to keep the inhaler in the car. / The pharmacist told us to keep the inhaler at room temperature. / The pharmacist told us to use the old inhaler.

    Answer / teacher checkb

Fill in the Blank

Write to or not.

  1. Direct: "Call if her breathing gets worse." Reported: He asked us ___ call if her breathing got worse.
    Answer / teacher checkto
  2. Look at step 3 on the sheet. The pharmacist told us ___ to use the old inhaler.
    Answer / teacher checknot

Unscramble

  1. Unscramble:
    Answer / teacher checkThe pharmacist told us not to leave it in the car

She Asked If…

Wednesday, 2 PM. Clinic receptionist Sarah called back about Amina's follow-up. Luz was at work, so Marco answered. He wrote Sarah's questions on a list. A ✅ means he answered it. A ⬜ means he must ask Luz.

Clinic call
Sarah's questions for Marco
✅ Is Amina feeling better?
⬜ When can you come for the follow-up?
⬜ What time does Amina finish school?
⬜ Did you bring the new insurance card last time?

Yes/no questions become asked if + statement (no question word order). Wh-questions keep the question word: asked when / what / where + statement.

yes/no Direct: "Is she feeling better?" → She asked if she was feeling better.
wh-question Direct: "When can you come?" → She asked when we could come.

Report the Question

Choose the correct reported question.

  1. Sarah asked: "What time does Amina finish school?" How does Marco report this?

    Sarah asked what time does Amina finish school. / Sarah asked what time Amina finished school. / Sarah asked what time Amina finishes school?

    Answer / teacher checkb
  2. Look at the list. Marco must ask Luz about the follow-up. How does he report Sarah's question?

    Sarah asked when could we come for the follow-up. / Sarah asked when we could come for the follow-up. / Sarah asked if when we could come for the follow-up.

    Answer / teacher checkb

Fill in the Blank

Write if or a number.

  1. Direct: "Did you bring the insurance card?" Reported: She asked ___ we had brought the insurance card.
    Answer / teacher checkif
  2. Look at the list. How many of Sarah's questions did Marco already answer? Write a number.
    Answer / teacher check1,one

Find the Error

Which reported question is NOT correct?

  1. Which sentence has an error?

    She asked if Amina was feeling better. / She asked when we could come for the follow-up. / She asked if did we bring the insurance card.

    Answer / teacher checkc

One Whole Story

Scene  Marco's break room. Wednesday, 9 PM. Photo: The Yardcoworking / Unsplash

Marco calls his mother Lucia in Guatemala on his break. He has to explain, in his own words, what three different people told him.

👨🏽
Marco
Mamá, the nurse said that Amina's inhaler was almost empty.
👵🏽
Lucia
Ay, mijo. And the pharmacy?
👨🏽
Marco
The pharmacist told me to keep it at room temperature. He told us not to use the old machine.
👵🏽
Lucia
Good. Tell Amina to call me after school. When is her next appointment?
👨🏽
Marco
Sarah asked when we could come back. I said that Saturday might work. We’re waiting to hear.

Statements, commands, and questions. All three patterns in one real phone call.

Want to go deeper?: This was the quick version. If you want more examples, more exercises, and the full explanation, open the Reported Speech Full Guide (app reference).

Statements, Commands, or Questions?

Choose the correct reported form for each situation.

  1. Kelly said: "The pharmacy can refill it today."

    Kelly said that the pharmacy could refill it today. / Kelly told me to refill it today. / Kelly asked if the pharmacy could refill it today.

    Answer / teacher checka
  2. The pharmacist said: "Don't use the old inhaler."

    The pharmacist said that we don't use the old inhaler. / The pharmacist told us not to use the old inhaler. / The pharmacist asked if we use the old inhaler.

    Answer / teacher checkb

Fill in the Blank

Write the missing word.

  1. Sarah asked: "When can you come?" Marco said Sarah asked ___ we could come.
    Answer / teacher checkwhen

Unscramble

  1. Unscramble Marco's sentence to Lucia:
    Answer / teacher checkHe told me to keep the inhaler at room temperature

Find the Error

  1. Marco texts Luz: "Sarah asked when can we come Saturday." What is wrong?

    No error. The sentence is correct. / Error: it should be "Sarah asked when we could come Saturday." / Error: it should be "Sarah said when we could come Saturday."

    Answer / teacher checkb

Guide mini-quiz

  1. Kelly said: "The new inhaler is ready." How does Luz report this to Marco?

    Kelly said that the new inhaler ready. / Kelly said that the new inhaler was ready. / Kelly told me to the new inhaler was ready.

    AnswerKelly said that the new inhaler was ready.

    In reported statements, is becomes was. Use said that + subject + verb.

  2. Sarah said: "Bring the new insurance card to the follow-up." How does Marco tell Luz?

    Sarah told me to bring the new insurance card to the follow-up. / Sarah said that bring the new insurance card to the follow-up. / Sarah asked me bring the new insurance card to the follow-up.

    AnswerSarah told me to bring the new insurance card to the follow-up.

    Commands use told + person + to + base verb.

  3. Fill in the blank: "Kelly said: 'We can refill it today.' → Kelly said that they ___ refill it today." (can back-shifts in reported speech)
    Answercould

    Can back-shifts to could in reported speech.

  4. Find the error. Luz is talking about last week: "Kelly said that the pharmacy will refill it the next day."

    No error. / Error: will should be would. / Error: said should be told.

    AnswerError: will should be would.

    Kelly spoke in the past about a time that is now past, so will back-shifts to would: Kelly said the pharmacy would refill it the next day.

  5. Marco reports what the pharmacist said about Amina's inhaler. Put the words in order.
    AnswerThe pharmacist told me to keep the inhaler inside

    Commands in reported speech use told + person + to + base verb.

Week 30 Quiz · required
  1. sit → V1-s (he/she/it)
    Answersits

    V1-s (he/she/it) of sit: sits.

  2. sit → V-ing
    Answersitting

    V-ing of sit: sitting.

  3. sit → V2 (past)
    Answersat

    V2 (past) of sit: sat.

  4. sit → V3 (past participle)
    Answersat

    V3 (past participle) of sit: sat.

  5. stand → V1-s (he/she/it)
    Answerstands

    V1-s (he/she/it) of stand: stands.

  6. stand → V-ing
    Answerstanding

  7. stand → V2 (past)
    Answerstood

    V2 (past) of stand: stood.

  8. stand → V3 (past participle)
    Answerstood

    V3 (past participle) of stand: stood.

  9. The nurse said she ___ beside me during the test. (sit: simple past)
    Answersat

  10. The doctor said I should ___ up slowly. (stand)
    Answerstand

  11. Which word means “to do physical activity to stay healthy”?

    improve / exercise / recover

  14. Marco reports what the pharmacist said about Amina's inhaler. Put the words in order. Words: The / pharmacist / told / me / to / keep / the / inhaler / inside

W31: Third Conditional: What Would Have Happened

Weekly plan ·

Required lesson and practice

If I Had Come Sooner

Scene  Walk-in clinic, East Boston. Saturday, 7:30 AM. Photo: Hush Naidoo Jade Photography / Unsplash

Yemi works as a packer at a warehouse in Chelsea. Three weeks ago she hurt her knee lifting a pallet. She kept working double shifts instead of resting. Now the pain is much worse, and she finally came to the clinic. Ms. Patel is the nurse practitioner.

👩🏽
Ms. Patel
How long has your knee been hurting?
👩🏿
Yemi
About three weeks. I know I waited too long.
👩🏿
Yemi
If I had come sooner, maybe I wouldn’t have missed so much work.
👩🏽
Ms. Patel
Let's take a look. Can you bend it for me?

Third conditional = you talk about a past choice and a different past result that did not happen. You cannot change it now, but you can say what would have been different.

did not happen If I had come sooner, I wouldn't have missed so much work. (She did not come sooner. She missed work.)
past regret If I had rested my knee, I would have kept working normal shifts.

Timeline labels: if + had + V3 (missed action) (past-earlier) → would have + V3 (different result) (past-later)

What does this sentence mean?

Choose the best meaning.

  1. "If I had come sooner, I wouldn't have missed so much work." What is true?

    Yemi came sooner and didn't miss any work. / Yemi did not come sooner, and she missed a lot of work. / Yemi will come to the clinic tomorrow.

    Answer / teacher checkb

Fill in the blank

Write the missing word.

  1. If I ___ rested my knee, it would have healed faster.
    Answer / teacher checkhad

Unscramble

  1. Unscramble:
    Answer / teacher checkIf she had asked for help, she would have missed less work

Building the Sentence

On Saturday afternoon, Yemi sits at her kitchen table and makes a list. The list shows four things she did not do in the last three weeks. Every box is empty.

Yemi's list
Things I did NOT do
⬜ Rest my knee
⬜ Ice it every night
⬜ Call the clinic
⬜ Take a day off work

If + had + past participle, would have + past participle. The word had is required in the if-clause. Do not skip it.

if-clause If I had called the clinic... (not "If I called")
result ...they would have told me to rest. (tell → told = past participle)
formula If + had + V3, would have + V3

Timeline labels: if + had + V3 (past-earlier) → would have + V3 (past-later)

Look at Yemi's list

Read the list, then answer.

  1. How many boxes on Yemi's list are checked?
    Answer / teacher check0,zero,none
  2. Look at the list. Yemi did not ice her knee. Which sentence is correct?

    If I iced it every night, it might have gotten better. / If I had iced it every night, it might have gotten better. / If I had ice it every night, it might have gotten better.

    Answer / teacher checkb

Use the list

Look at the third box. Write two words.

  1. If I ___ the clinic, they would have told me to rest. (call)
    Answer / teacher checkhad called

Spot the error

  1. "If I called the clinic last week, I wouldn't have missed three shifts." What is wrong?

    No error. The sentence is correct. / Error: should be "If I had called" (missing had). / Error: should be "I wouldn't miss" not "wouldn't have missed".

    Answer / teacher checkb

Unscramble

  1. Unscramble:
    Answer / teacher checkIf I had taken a day off, my knee would have felt better

Three Shifts and a Bigger Bill

Because Yemi waited, her knee got worse. Look at the table. The left side is what really happened. The right side is what would have happened if she had gone to the clinic sooner.

Table
Yemi: real life and a different past
Really happened Would have happened
She missed 3 shifts. She wouldn't have missed 3 shifts.
She lost almost $400. She would have kept that money.
The clinic bill was $80. The bill might have been smaller.

Negative results: wouldn't have + past participle. You can also use could have or might have for a less certain result.

negative If I had gone sooner, I wouldn't have missed three shifts.
could have You could have called the nurse line. (possible, but you did not)

Look at the table

Read the table, then choose.

  1. Look at the table. How many shifts did Yemi really miss?

    0 / 3 / 80

    Answer / teacher checkb
  2. Look at the table. "If Yemi had gone sooner, she ___ almost $400."

    wouldn't lose / wouldn't have lost / didn't lose

    Answer / teacher checkb

Fill in the blank

Write one word.

  1. Yemi lost almost $400. "If I had gone sooner, I wouldn't ___ lost that money."
    Answer / teacher checkhave

Unscramble

  1. Unscramble:
    Answer / teacher checkIf Yemi had gone sooner, she would have kept her money

Imaginary Now vs. Imaginary Past

On the bus, Yemi reads about a scientist who left home to study in another country. His story is all in the past, so we can only imagine a different past for it. Yemi's bill is different: she can still call the clinic today.

Earth Day
Mario Molina: The Scientist Who Warned About the Ozone Layer

Mario Molina was born in Mexico City. He studied chemical engineering at the National Autonomous University of Mexico (UNAM), then went to the University of California, Berkeley, for graduate school. Later, he joined F. Sherwood Rowland's research group at UC Irvine.

In 1974, Molina and Rowland wrote an article that warned about gases called CFCs. They said CFCs could damage the ozone layer. In 1995, Molina, Rowland, and Paul Crutzen won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry. In 2013, President Obama gave Molina the Presidential Medal of Freedom. Molina died in 2020.

Photo: Janwikifoto, 2011, CC BY-SA 3.0. Sources: University of California Academic Senate, Science History Institute, UC San Diego Today

Molina's past cannot change, so a different past is only imagination. Here is the grammar:

Second conditional: If + past simple, would + base verb. Imaginary now.
Third conditional: If + had + V3, would have + V3. Imaginary past.

second (now) If Yemi called the clinic now, they would help her. (Still possible.)
third (past) If Yemi had called three weeks ago, she wouldn't have missed three shifts. (Too late.)

Timeline labels: Second: would (imaginary now) (past) → Third: if + had + V3 (past-earlier) → Third: would have + V3 (past-later)

Read about Mario Molina

Read the card, then answer.

  1. Which sentence about Mario Molina is true?

    He was born in Germany. / He went to Berkeley for graduate school. / He won the Nobel Prize in 1974.

    Answer / teacher checkb
  2. How many years passed between the 1974 article and the Nobel Prize? (number)
    Answer / teacher check21,twenty-one,twenty one

Second or third?

Choose the correct conditional based on the situation.

  1. Yemi can still call the clinic today about the bill. "If I ___ the clinic, they would help me."

    called (second conditional, still possible) / had called (third conditional, past only)

    Answer / teacher checka
  2. Imagine a different past (our guess, not history). Which sentence is correct?

    If Molina and Rowland hadn't written the article in 1974, people might not have learned about CFCs so soon. / If Molina and Rowland didn't write the article in 1974, people might not have learned about CFCs so soon. / If Molina and Rowland hadn't written the article in 1974, people might not learn about CFCs so soon.

    Answer / teacher checka

Fill in the blank

Write would or would have.

  1. If I called the clinic now, they ___ help me. (imaginary now)
    Answer / teacher checkwould
  2. If I had rested three weeks ago, I ___ saved almost $400. (past regret)
    Answer / teacher checkwould have

What Would Have Happened? One Whole Story

Scene  Warehouse break room. Wednesday, before the shift. Photo: Resume Genius / Unsplash

Yemi and Jennifer talk before their shift. Jennifer remembers a coworker who got hurt last year.

👩🏻
Jennifer
Remember Kevin last year? If he'd used the lift, he wouldn't have hurt his back.
👩🏿
Yemi
Same idea with my knee. If I had rested when it started, I wouldn't have missed three shifts.
👩🏻
Jennifer
And if you called the nurse line now, they'd tell you what to do next.
👩🏿
Yemi
You're right. I can't change the past. But I can call today.

That evening, Yemi calls the nurse line. The nurse tells her to rest and ice the knee. On the way home, she stops at the pharmacy for a knee brace. The pharmacist shows her how to put it on and says, "If you had come in three weeks ago, I could have shown you this then."

Third conditional for past regrets. Second conditional when you can still act.

Want to go deeper?: This was the quick version. For more examples, all four conditionals side by side, and extra practice, open the Second and Third Conditionals Full Guide (app reference).

Pick the right pattern

Statement, negative, or second vs. third?

  1. Yemi did not rest her knee three weeks ago.

    If I had rested my knee, it would have healed faster. / If I rested my knee, it would heal faster. / If I rest my knee, it will heal faster.

    Answer / teacher checka
  2. Jennifer talks about Kevin's accident last year.

    If he used the lift, he isn't injured. / If he had used the lift, he wouldn't have been injured. / If he has used the lift, he wouldn't have been injured.

    Answer / teacher checkb

What really happened?

Choose the best meaning.

  1. Jennifer says: "If Kevin had used the lift, he wouldn't have hurt his back." What is true?

    Kevin used the lift and did not get hurt. / Kevin did not use the lift, and he got hurt. / Kevin will use the lift tomorrow.

    Answer / teacher checkb
  2. Last month a coworker did not wear gloves, and he cut his hand. If he ___ (wear) gloves, he wouldn't have cut his hand.
    Answer / teacher checkhad worn,'d worn

Unscramble

  1. Unscramble:
    Answer / teacher checkIf he had used the lift, he wouldn't have been injured

Spot the error

  1. Yemi says: "If I had called three weeks ago, I wouldn't miss three shifts." What is wrong?

    No error. / Error: should be "wouldn't have missed" (past result needs would have + V3). / Error: should be "If I called" without had.

    Answer / teacher checkb

Guide mini-quiz

  1. Yemi did not rest her knee when it started to hurt, and it got worse. Which sentence matches her situation?

    If I rest my knee, it won't get worse. / If I had rested my knee, it wouldn't have gotten worse. / If I rested my knee, it wouldn't get worse.

    AnswerIf I had rested my knee, it wouldn't have gotten worse.

    Third conditional uses if + had + V3 for a past action that did not happen.

  2. Which sentence is a correct third conditional?

    If Yemi rested more, she will have healed faster. / If Yemi had rested more, she would have healed faster. / If Yemi has rested more, she would heal faster.

    AnswerIf Yemi had rested more, she would have healed faster.

    Third conditional: if + had + V3, would have + V3.

  3. Fill in the blank: "If I had rested my knee, I ___ $80." (a different past result that didn't happen)
    Answerwouldn't have paid

    A past result that did not happen uses wouldn't have + past participle.

  4. Find the error: "If Yemi had went to the clinic sooner, she would have paid less."

    No error. / Error: should be "had gone" (the past participle of go is gone). / Error: should be "she would pay" not "she would have paid".

    AnswerError: should be "had gone" (the past participle of go is gone).

    After had, use the past participle: had gone, not had went.

  5. Yemi regrets waiting to go to the clinic. Put the words in order.
    AnswerIf I had gone sooner I would have paid less

    Third conditional: if + had gone (past), would have paid (past result that didn't happen).

W32: Future Perfect: Goals and Milestones

Weekly plan ·

Required lesson and practice

Finished by a future date

Beatriz works in a restaurant. She is making a small walking plan with her coworker Sarah.

Beatriz: By the end of May, I will have completed my walking plan.

Sarah: By Friday, I will have finished my activity log.

Now → work on the goal → finished by the deadline

Timeline labels: will have finished (future) → future deadline (future)

Try the pattern

  1. By Friday, Sarah ___ (finish) her activity log. Use will have + past participle.
    Answer / teacher checkwill have finished

Build the sentence

Subject + will have + past participle (V3).

Use familiar V3 forms: finished, completed, written, done. The helper words stay the same for every subject.

By Sunday, Tuan will have written his plan for the next week.

Timeline labels: will have written (future) → future deadline (future)

Try the pattern

  1. By Sunday, Tuan ___ (write) his plan. Use the future perfect.
    Answer / teacher checkwill have written

A plan or a completed milestone?

I am going to write my plan tonight. This tells us my intention.

By tomorrow, I will have written my plan. This looks back from a future deadline at the completed result.

By Friday means no later than Friday. A by-phrase does not always require the future perfect; today we are practicing that form.

Timeline labels: will have completed (future) → future deadline (future)

Try the pattern

  1. By the end of May, Beatriz ___ (complete) her walking plan. Use the future perfect.
    Answer / teacher checkwill have completed

Your next small milestone

Choose a realistic goal: finish a plan, write a list, complete a class activity. Tell a partner: By ___, I will have ___.

Keep the goal small enough to fit around work and family. A complete practice attempt earns effort credit; check and revise after feedback.

Timeline labels: will have done (future) → future deadline (future)

Try the pattern

  1. By Thursday, I ___ (do) my English homework. Use the future perfect.
    Answer / teacher checkwill have done

W33: Be Used to / Get Used to

Weekly plan ·

Required lesson and practice

I'm Used to Working Nights

Bring back: Bring back W21: I used to work nights = a past habit. I am used to working nights = it feels familiar now. Notice that the to in be used to is followed by a noun or -ing.

Scene  Restaurant kitchen, East Boston. A Tuesday in November, 11 PM. Photo: Angelina Kusznirewicz / Unsplash

Fabienne moved to East Boston from Haiti last summer. She has two kids, and she works nights as a prep cook at a restaurant. Her supervisor Mark checks in before close.

🧑‍💼
Mark
Long night again. How do you handle closing every Tuesday?
👩🏾
Fabienne
I'm used to finishing at midnight. The first month was hard.
🧑‍💼
Mark
You're fast on the line now.
👩🏾
Fabienne
Yeah. I'm used to working nights. It feels normal.

Be used to + gerund = something feels familiar or normal now. Not the same as used to + verb from Week 21 (that was a past habit that changed).

formula am / is / are + used to + verb-ing (or a noun)
familiar now I'm used to working nights. (It feels normal now.)
with noun She's used to the schedule. (No -ing after a noun.)

Timeline labels: am/is/are used to + -ing (present)

What does be used to mean?

Choose the best answer.

  1. "I'm used to working nights." What is true now?

    Fabienne worked nights in the past but stopped. / Working nights feels familiar to Fabienne now. / Fabienne will start working nights next month.

    Answer / teacher checkb

Fill in the blank

Write am, is, or are.

  1. I ___ used to finishing at midnight.
    Answer / teacher checkam

Unscramble

  1. Build a sentence about Fabienne's routine:
    Answer / teacher checkI'm used to sleeping in the afternoon

I'm Not Used to the Cold Yet

It is January, and it is Fabienne's first winter in Boston. After closing, she waits for the bus at 12:30 AM and makes a list on her phone. A checked box means she is used to it. An empty box means she is not used to it yet.

Fabienne's first winter
Used to it yet? (January)
✅ Working nights (since October)
✅ Sleeping in the afternoon
✅ Finishing at midnight
⬜ Waiting outside for the bus
⬜ Switching buses in the dark

Negative: am / is / are + not + used to + gerund. Something still feels uncomfortable or unfamiliar now.

not yet I'm not used to waiting in the cold. (Still hard.)
past habit I used to walk to work. (Different grammar. Past only.)

Read Fabienne's list

Look at the checklist. Choose the sentence that is true.

    Answer / teacher checkb

    Answer / teacher check3,three
  3. In Haiti, Fabienne walked to work every day. She does not do that now. Which sentence is correct?

Fill in the blank

Write the -ing form.

  1. Fabienne is not used to ___ (ride) the bus at night.
    Answer / teacher checkriding

Spot the error

  1. "I'm not used to wait outside this long." What is wrong?

    No error. / Error: should be "not used to waiting" (-ing after be used to). / Error: should be "didn't use to wait".

    Answer / teacher checkb

I'm Getting Used to School Emails

Here are Fabienne's first six months in East Boston. Some things became normal. Some things are still changing. In February, her kids' school sends a health form on ParentSquare, and she reads it on her phone at the bus stop.

Fabienne's first months
From August to February

Fabienne moves to East Boston from Haiti.
2 months

She starts her first night shift at the restaurant.
1 month

She is used to finishing at midnight. It feels normal.
2 months
Jan

1 month

She reads some school emails twice. She is getting used to reading them in English.

Get used to + gerund = the process of adapting. It is getting easier, but you are not fully comfortable yet.

in progress I'm getting used to reading school emails. (Still learning.)
familiar now I'm used to checking my phone after work. (Already normal.)

Timeline labels: getting used to + -ing (present)

Look at Fabienne's timeline. Choose the best answer.

Choose the best form for the meaning.

Write getting.

  1. I'm ___ used to reading school emails in English.
    Answer / teacher checkgetting

Three "Used To" Patterns: Don't Mix Them Up

May is Asian American and Pacific Islander Heritage Month. Many adult learners know a story like Fabienne's: a new country, a new language, a new life. Read about Mazie Hirono. The bold words are a past situation.

Asian American and Pacific Islander Heritage Month
Mazie Hirono: From a Rice Farm to the Senate

Mazie Hirono used to live in Fukushima, Japan. Her early childhood was spent on her grandparents' rice farm. When she was nearly eight years old, she, her mother, and her brother crossed the Pacific by ship and came to Hawaii.

When she began elementary school, she neither spoke nor read English. She studied in Hawaii's public schools, went to the University of Hawaii, and later went to law school at Georgetown. In 2013, she was sworn in as a U.S. senator. She became the first Asian American woman in the Senate.

Photo: U.S. Senate, public domain. Source: Senator Hirono's official biography

used to + verb = past habit, not true now.
be used to + -ing = familiar now.
get used to + -ing = still adapting.

past Fabienne used to sleep at night. (Not now. She works nights.)
familiar She's used to working nights.
adapting She's getting used to reading school emails.

Timeline labels: used to + verb (past habit) (past) → be used to + -ing (familiar now) (present) → getting used to + -ing (present)

Read about Mazie Hirono

Look at the reading. Answer the questions.

  1. Which sentence is correct? Mazie Hirono does not live in Japan now.

    She used to live in Japan. / She is used to live in Japan. / She used to living in Japan.

    Answer / teacher checka
  2. How old was Mazie when her family came to Hawaii? She was nearly ___ years old. Write a number.
    Answer / teacher check8,eight

Pick the right pattern

Choose the sentence that matches the meaning.

    She is used to reading school emails already. / She is getting used to reading school emails. / She used to reading school emails.

    Answer / teacher checkb

    No error. / Error: should be "used to waking up" (-ing after be used to). / Error: should be "used to wake up" (past habit).

    Answer / teacher checkb

Write used, used to, or getting.

  1. Fabienne ___ to sleep at night, but now she sleeps in the afternoon. (past habit)
    Answer / teacher checkused

Still Adjusting: One Hard Week

Scene  Restaurant break room. A Wednesday in March, 4 PM. Photo: Quilia / Unsplash

It has been a hard week for Fabienne: double shifts, English school emails, and now she needs Friday off for a parent-teacher meeting. Before her shift starts, she finds her supervisor Mark in the break room.

👩🏾
Fabienne
Hi Mark. Can I take Friday off? I have a parent-teacher meeting at 10.
🧑‍💼
Mark
Let me check the schedule. How are you holding up?
👩🏾
Fabienne
Tired. I’m still getting used to the double shifts. Could I make up the hours on Saturday?
🧑‍💼
Mark
OK, Friday's yours. Can you work Saturday, 4 to midnight?
👩🏾
Fabienne
Yes. I'm used to working late. Thank you, Mark!

    I'm used to eat dinner very late. / I'm used to eating dinner very late. / I used to eating dinner very late.

    AnswerI'm used to eating dinner very late.

  2. What does "getting used to" mean?

    Already fully comfortable / Still adapting, but it is getting easier / A habit from the past that ended

    AnswerStill adapting, but it is getting easier

    Getting used to shows the process of becoming accustomed.

  3. Fill in the blank: "I'm not used to ___ outside in January." (Fabienne still finds the cold bus stop hard.)
    Answerwaiting

  4. Find the error: "She is used to work nights."

    After be used to, use a gerund: working.

  5. Mark describes Fabienne's routine. Put the words in order.
    AnswerShe is used to working nights

    Be used to + gerund (working) means it feels familiar or normal now.

    coping skills: ways to handle stress or problems. Deep breathing is one of my coping skills for stress.

  17. Mark describes Fabienne's routine. Put the words in order. Words: She / is / used / to / working / nights
    AnswerShe is used to working nights

    Be used to + gerund (working) means it feels familiar or normal now.

  18. Fabienne eats dinner at 1 AM after her shift every night. Which sentence is correct?

    I'm used to eat dinner very late. / I'm used to eating dinner very late. / I used to eating dinner very late.

    AnswerI'm used to eating dinner very late.

    Be used to needs a gerund: eating, not eat.

W34: All Four Conditionals: A Quick Tour

Weekly plan ·

Required lesson and practice

If I Lift Wrong, My Knee Hurts

Bring back: Quick verb-pattern warm-up: I enjoy walking. I want to rest. I stopped working = the work ended. I stopped to rest = I paused another activity in order to rest.

Scene  Warehouse loading dock, Chelsea. Monday, 10 PM. Photo: Pickawood / Unsplash

Yemi is a packer at a warehouse in Chelsea. Last month she hurt her knee and missed three shifts. Now she is moving to nights, because they pay more. Tonight is her first night shift, so supervisor Brian reviews lifting rules before she goes back to pallets.

🧑🏼
Brian
Before you lift again, remember the rules. If you lift with your back, you hurt yourself.
👩🏿
Yemi
I know. I learned that the hard way.
🧑🏼
Brian
If you bend at the waist, you risk injury. Use your legs.
👩🏿
Yemi
OK. If I lift wrong, my knee hurts. Can you watch me try again?

Zero conditional = a fact or rule that is always true. Both verbs are present simple.
If + present, present.

always true If I lift wrong, my knee hurts.
rule If you bend at the waist, you risk injury.

Timeline labels: if + present (present) → result (present) (present)

Zero or first?

Choose the sentence that fits the meaning.

  1. Brian explains another safety rule that is always true. Which sentence fits?

    If you skip your break, you will get tired. / If you skip your break, you get tired. / If you skipped your break, you would get tired.

    Answer / teacher checkb
  2. Which sentence is the zero conditional?

    If the freezer door stays open, the food will spoil tonight. / If the freezer door stayed open, the food would spoil. / If the freezer door stays open, the food spoils.

    Answer / teacher checkc

Fill in the blank

Write the present simple verb.

  1. If you bend at the waist, you ___ (risk) injury.
    Answer / teacher checkrisk

Unscramble

  1. Build a zero conditional about Yemi's knee:
    Answer / teacher checkIf you lift wrong, your knee hurts

If the Clinic Opens at 8, I'll Go

After her first week of night shifts, Yemi needs a follow-up visit for her knee. Her coworker Rachel goes to the same clinic and tells her that walk-ins start at 8. Yemi writes her Saturday plan on her phone.

Yemi's phone note
Saturday plan for my knee
1 Plan A: If the clinic opens at 8, I'll go first thing.
2 Plan A: If the line is short, I'll be back by noon.
3 Plan B: If they can't see me, I'll try the walk-in downtown.
4 If the doctor gives me a note, I'll bring it to work on Monday.
Bring: ID and insurance card.

First conditional = a real situation that might happen. The result is in the future.
If + present, will + base verb.

real plan If the clinic opens at 8, I'll go first thing.
not zero Zero = always true. First = might happen: I'll go, not I go.

Timeline labels: if + present (present) → will + verb (future)

Read Yemi's plan

Look at Yemi's phone note above. Then answer.

  1. Which place is Yemi's Plan B?

    The walk-in clinic downtown / Her warehouse / Rachel's apartment

    Answer / teacher checka
  2. When will Yemi bring the doctor's note to work?

    On Saturday / On Monday / At noon

    Answer / teacher checkb

First or zero?

Pick the correct form.

  1. After the clinic, Yemi has a real plan for the bus ride home. Which sentence fits?

    If the bus comes on time, I'll get home by noon. / If the bus comes on time, I get home by noon. / If the bus came on time, I would get home by noon.

    Answer / teacher checka
  2. Find the error: "If the clinic will open at 8, I'll go."

    No error. / Error: no will in the if-clause. Should be "If the clinic opens..." / Error: should be "If the clinic opened..."

    Answer / teacher checkb

Fill in the blank

Write 'll or will.

  1. If the bus is late, I ___ call my sister.
    Answer / teacher check'll,will

Unscramble

  1. Build a plan for a rainy Saturday:
    Answer / teacher checkIf it rains tomorrow, I'll take the bus

If I Had Day Shifts, I Would Sleep More

Yemi's night shift starts at 7 PM, but her kids go to bed at 8:30 PM. On break, Rachel asks about her schedule. Here is Yemi's real week.

Yemi's week
Night shifts and kids' bedtime
Mon Tue Wed Thu Fri Sat Sun
Night shift starts
7pm
7pm
7pm
7pm
7pm
7pm
 ·
Kids' bedtime
8:30
8:30
8:30
8:30
8:30
8:30
8:30
Home at bedtime?
No
No
No
No
No
No
Yes
Yemi works Monday to Saturday. She is home at bedtime only on Sunday.

Second conditional = an imaginary situation now. The verb after if looks like past tense, but it is not about the real past.
If + past simple, would + base verb.

imaginary If I had day shifts, I would sleep more. (She has night shifts.)
not first First = real plan (I'll go). Second = wish (I would sleep).

Timeline labels: if + past simple (imaginary) (past) → would + verb (imaginary) (future)

Read Yemi's week

Look at the schedule above. Then answer.

  1. On which day is Yemi home at bedtime?

    Monday / Wednesday / Saturday / Sunday

    Answer / teacher checkd
  2. Yemi works on Saturday. Which imaginary sentence is correct?

    If Yemi had Saturday off, she would be home at bedtime. / If Yemi has Saturday off, she would be home at bedtime. / If Yemi would have Saturday off, she is home at bedtime.

    Answer / teacher checka

Second or first?

Choose the best form.

  1. Yemi lives an hour from the warehouse. She does not live closer. Which sentence fits her wish?

    If I live closer, I'll save an hour every day. / If I had lived closer, I would have saved an hour. / If I lived closer, I would save an hour every day.

    Answer / teacher checkc
  2. Find the error: "If I would have day shifts, I would sleep more."

    No error. / Error: no would in the if-clause. Should be "If I had day shifts..." / Error: should be "If I have day shifts..."

    Answer / teacher checkb

Fill in the blank

Write the verb.

  1. If Yemi ___ (have) Saturday off, she would be home at bedtime.
    Answer / teacher checkhad

Unscramble

  1. Build Yemi's wish about her Saturdays:
    Answer / teacher checkIf I had Saturdays off, I would see my kids more

If I Had Gone Sooner, I Would Have Paid Less

Scene  Clinic billing desk, East Boston. Saturday, 10 AM. Photo: Martha Dominguez de Gouveia / Unsplash

After her follow-up visit, Yemi sees the copay and thinks about the shifts she missed by waiting too long. Lisa at the front desk helps her with the bill.

👩🏿
Yemi
If I had called the clinic right away, I wouldn't have missed three shifts.
👩🏽
Lisa
I can set up a payment plan for the copay.
👩🏿
Yemi
Thanks. I’m just worried about the money. If I had gone sooner, I wouldn’t have lost so much in wages.

Third conditional = a past choice and a different past result that did not happen. You cannot change it now.
If + past perfect, would have + V3.

did not happen If I had gone sooner, I would have paid less. (She went late.)
not second Second = had + base verb (now). Third = had gone / had called (past).

Timeline labels: if + had + V3 (past-earlier) → would have + V3 (past-later)

Third or second?

Choose the correct form.

  1. Last month Yemi lifted a heavy box alone and hurt her knee. Which sentence fits her regret?

    If I asked for help, I wouldn't hurt my knee. / If I ask for help, I don't hurt my knee. / If I had asked for help, I wouldn't have hurt my knee.

    Answer / teacher checkc
  2. Find the error: "If I would have gone sooner, I would have paid less."

    No error. / Error: no would in the if-clause. Should be "If I had gone sooner..." / Error: should be "If I had day shifts..."

    Answer / teacher checkb

Fill in the blank

Write had.

  1. If I ___ gone sooner, I would have paid less.
    Answer / teacher checkhad

Unscramble

  1. Build Yemi's regret about her knee:
    Answer / teacher checkIf I had rested my knee, I would have healed faster

One Bad Week: All Four Together

Yemi's hard week had all four conditionals: a sore knee, a clinic visit, and her first night shifts. Here are her sentences in one table. Read it from top to bottom.

Compare
Yemi's week: four conditionals
Type If part Result
Zero
always true 		If I lift wrong, my knee hurts.
First
real plan 		If the clinic opens at 8, I'll go first thing.
Second
imaginary now 		If I had day shifts, I would sleep more.
Third
imaginary past 		If I had gone sooner, I wouldn't have missed three shifts.

Zero = if + present, present
First = if + present, will
Second = if + past, would
Third = if + had + V3, would have + V3

Want to go deeper?: This was the quick tour. For full explanations and more practice, open the Zero + First Conditionals Full Guide (app reference) and the Second and Third Conditionals Full Guide (app reference).

Read the table

Look at the table above. Then answer.

  1. Which row is a real plan for the future?

    Zero / First / Second / Third

    Answer / teacher checkb
  2. Which row has a result with "would have" + V3?

    Zero / First / Second / Third

    Answer / teacher checkd
  3. Which sentence has the same pattern as the Second row?

    If I lived closer, I would walk to work. / If I live closer, I'll walk to work. / If I had lived closer, I would have walked to work. / If I live closer, I walk to work.

    Answer / teacher checka

Pick the right conditional

Read each situation and match the meaning.

  1. In a kitchen, a safety rule that is always true.

    If you touched the grill, you would burn your hand. / If you touch the grill, you will burn your hand. / If you touch the grill, you burn your hand. / If you had touched the grill, you would have burned your hand.

    Answer / teacher checkc
  2. A real plan for payday on Friday.

    If I get paid Friday, I'll buy my monthly bus pass. / If I got paid Friday, I would buy my monthly bus pass. / If I get paid Friday, I buy my monthly bus pass. / If I had been paid Friday, I would have bought my monthly bus pass.

    Answer / teacher checka
  3. Your apartment is an hour from work. Your wish (not real now).

    If I live near work, I'll walk every day. / If I live near work, I walk every day. / If I had lived near work, I would have walked every day. / If I lived near work, I would walk every day.

    Answer / teacher checkd
  4. Last winter you skipped the flu shot and got sick. Your regret.

    If I get the flu shot, I don't get sick. / If I had gotten the flu shot, I wouldn't have been sick for a week. / If I got the flu shot, I wouldn't be sick. / If I will get the flu shot, I won't be sick.

    Answer / teacher checkb

Spot the error

  1. Which sentence has an error?

    If you touch a hot pan, you get burned. / If I get paid Friday, I'll pay the rent. / If I would have a car, I would drive to work. / If I had left earlier, I would have caught the bus.

    Answer / teacher checkc

    Answer / teacher checkIf I had called the clinic, I would have gotten help sooner

Guide mini-quiz

  1. Yemi has a real plan for after her follow-up visit on Saturday. Which sentence fits?

    If the doctor gives me a note, I'll bring it to work on Monday. / If the doctor gives me a note, I bring it to work on Monday. / If the doctor gave me a note, I would bring it to work. / If the doctor had given me a note, I would have brought it to work.

    AnswerIf the doctor gives me a note, I'll bring it to work on Monday.

    Real future plan = first conditional: if + present, will.

  2. Yemi says: 'If I earned more, I would move to a bigger apartment.' What do we know about Yemi?

    She earns enough and is moving soon. / She moved to a bigger apartment last year. / She does not earn enough now. The move is imaginary. / She will earn more next month for sure.

    AnswerShe does not earn enough now. The move is imaginary.

    Second conditional describes an imaginary situation now. The past-looking verb (earned) does not mean real past.

  3. Brian posts a rule in the break room. It is always true. Complete it: "If the warehouse door stays open, the loading dock ___ (get) cold."
    Answergets

    Zero conditional: if + present simple, present simple. Used for facts and rules.

  4. Find the error: "If I would have asked for lighter boxes, I would not have hurt my knee."

    No error. The sentence is correct. / The if-part should be "If I had asked for lighter boxes". / The if-part should be "If I ask for lighter boxes". / The result should be "I will not hurt my knee".

    AnswerThe if-part should be "If I had asked for lighter boxes".

    Third conditional never uses would in the if-part: if + had + V3, would have + V3.

  5. Yemi does not have a car. She imagines a different life. Put the words in order to build her sentence.
    AnswerIf I had a car I would drive to work

    Second conditional uses if + past simple for imaginary situations now.

W35: Future Perfect Continuous: Looking Back from June

Weekly plan ·

Required lesson and practice

How long by then?

Fabienne started this English class in September. She talks with her classmate Michael before their June class.

Fabienne: By June, I will have been studying here for about nine months.

Michael: By June, I will have been working at the restaurant for a year.

Start → activity continues through now → count its duration at a future point

Timeline labels: will have been studying (future) → future deadline (future)

Try the pattern

  1. By June, Fabienne ___ (study) here for about nine months. Use will have been + -ing.
    Answer / teacher checkwill have been studying

Build the sentence in chunks

Subject | will have been | verb-ing | for + duration.

Michael | will have been | working | for a year.

Keep the helper words together. They do not change with the subject. Start with familiar activities such as working, studying, and practicing.

Timeline labels: will have been working (future) → future deadline (future)

Try the pattern

  1. By June, Michael ___ (work) at the restaurant for a year. Use the future perfect continuous.
    Answer / teacher checkwill have been working

Finished result or duration?

W32: By June, I will have completed the course. Focus: the finished result.

Today: By June, I will have been studying for about nine months. Focus: how long the activity has continued up to that future point.

W25 counts duration up to now. W26 counts duration up to a past event. Today we count up to a future point.

Timeline labels: will have been practicing (future) → future deadline (future)

Try the pattern

  1. By Friday, Lan ___ (practice) her presentation for two weeks. Emphasize duration with the future perfect continuous.
    Answer / teacher checkwill have been practicing

Say one sentence about progress

Use a real or imagined activity with a clear starting point: By ___, I will have been ___ for ___.

Say the helper words slowly, then add the activity and duration. A complete attempt earns effort credit; use feedback to revise.

Timeline labels: will have been learning (future) → future deadline (future)

Try the pattern

  1. By next month, I ___ (learn) English for a year. Use the future perfect continuous.
    Answer / teacher checkwill have been learning

W36: All the Tenses: A Year in Review

Weekly plan ·

Required lesson and practice

One Year, One Timeline

Scene  East Boston evening ESOL class. Thursday, June 5, 7 PM. Photo: Карина Низаметдинова / Unsplash

Ms. Tran stands at the front of the room. It is the last class of the year. She asks the class about their plans for the fall.

👩‍🏫
Ms. Tran
It's our last night together. What will you do in the fall?
👩🏽
Rosa
I will enroll in Level 4 in September. I just need to make sure it fits around my work schedule.
👨🏻
David
Same here. I work construction all day. Two evenings a week is all I can do.
👩🏽
Rosa
And we're both going to take the free online summer course in July.

Your year, one timeline. Every tense on this timeline is one you practiced this year.

Simple = fact or finished. Continuous = in progress. Perfect = connected to a reference point. Past perfect = before another past event. Will / going to = the future.

every Tuesday I take the 116 every Tuesday.
right now I am sitting in class right now.
in July I am going to take the summer course in July.

Timeline labels: Past Perfect (past-earlier) → Past Cont. (past) → Past Simple (past) → Pres. Simple (present) → Pres. Cont. (present) → Pres. Perfect (past) → Pres. Perf. Cont. (past) → will / going to (future)

Which sentence fits?

Read the time indicator, then pick the best sentence.

  1. Rosa's schedule: she goes to class <strong>every Tuesday and Thursday</strong>.

    She is taking class every Tuesday and Thursday. / She takes class every Tuesday and Thursday. / She took class every Tuesday and Thursday.

    Answer / teacher checkb
  2. Right now, Rosa <strong>is in class</strong> and her phone is on silent.

    She sits in class and her phone is on silent. / She is sitting in class and her phone is on silent. / She has sat in class and her phone is on silent.

    Answer / teacher checkb
  3. Rosa has a plan. In July, she ___ (take) the online summer course. Use going to.
    Answer / teacher checkis going to take,'s going to take

Every Tuesday vs. Right Now

Rosa is a housekeeper at a hotel on Meridian Street. Her supervisor, Jennifer, helps her when she needs to leave early. This is Rosa's regular week.

Schedule
Rosa's regular week
Mon Tue Wed Thu Fri
🏨 Hotel work
7-3
7-3
7-3
7-3
7-3
📚 ESOL class
·
6 pm

6 pm

🛎️ Jennifer covers the late checkouts
· ·
Jen
 · ·

Now it is Wednesday afternoon, and Rosa is on her break. Right now she is texting the babysitter about picking up her daughter.

Present Simple = routines and facts. Present Continuous = happening right now or this week.

routine I work at the hotel Monday through Friday.
right now I am texting the babysitter about the pickup.

Timeline labels: Present Simple (present) → Present Continuous (present)

Simple or continuous?

Look at Rosa's regular week. Then pick the form that fits.

  1. Look at Rosa's week. Which sentence is true?

    Rosa takes class on Wednesday. / Rosa takes class on Tuesday and Thursday. / Rosa takes class on Monday and Friday.

    Answer / teacher checkb
  2. Hold on. Rosa ___ the babysitter right now. (text)

    texts / is texting / has texted

    Answer / teacher checkis texting
  3. Look at the schedule. Jennifer usually ___ (cover) the late checkouts on Wednesdays.
    Answer / teacher checkcovers
  4. Look at the schedule. How many days a week does Rosa work at the hotel? (Write a number.)
    Answer / teacher check5,five

Unscramble

  1. Unscramble:
    Answer / teacher checkRosa starts work at 7 on weekdays

What Happened, What Was Already Done

For the last class, Ms. Tran gives everyone a reading about a singer. Rosa reads it on the 116 bus. Look for three kinds of past: what happened, what was in progress, and what had already finished.

A real life
Gloria Estefan

Gloria Estefan was a toddler when her family fled Cuba. Her band, Miami Sound Machine, was traveling on a snowy highway in Pennsylvania in March 1990 when their bus had an accident with a tractor-trailer. Gloria broke a bone in her back, and surgeons operated on her spine for four hours.

She did not give up. Before she returned to performing in January 1991, she had done extensive physical therapy. By 2015, she had sold more than 100 million records, and she and her husband received the Presidential Medal of Freedom.

Photo: U.S. State Department, 2017, public domain. Sources: Biography.com, The White House (2015 Medal of Freedom)

Past Simple = finished event. Past Continuous = in progress when something else happened. Past Perfect = already finished before another past event.

Past perfect continuous: I had been working for two hours when the bus came. This focuses on duration up to a past event, as in W26.

in progress The band was traveling when the bus had an accident.
before that She had done physical therapy before she returned.

Timeline labels: Past Perfect (past-earlier) → Past Continuous (past) → Past Simple (past)

Pick the right past form

Read about Gloria Estefan again if you need to.

  1. The band ___ on a snowy highway when the bus had an accident. (travel)

    was traveling / traveled / had traveled

    Answer / teacher checkwas traveling
  2. Look at the reading. Which happened first?

    Gloria did physical therapy. / Gloria returned to performing.

    Answer / teacher checktherapy
  3. Look at the reading. By 2015, Gloria had sold more than ___ million records. (Write a number.)
    Answer / teacher check100
  4. Rosa ___ (already read) the article before the bus reached her stop.
    Answer / teacher checkhad already read

Bring back Week 26

  1. I ___ (work) for two hours when my break started. Use the past perfect continuous.
    Answer / teacher checkhad been working

Find the error

  1. "Her family <strong>has fled</strong> Cuba when she was a toddler."

    Correct as written / Should be 'fled' (past simple for a finished event) / Should be 'was fleeing' (past continuous)

    Answer / teacher checkfled

From September Until Now

After class, Rosa writes about her life for a class project. She puts the dates on a timeline. Today is June, and she looks at her timeline.

Timeline
Rosa's life in East Boston
2021
Rosa moved to East Boston.
3 years ago
She started working in housekeeping.
March
She began taking extra shifts.
since March
Now (June)
She is tired, but she is still working.

Present Perfect = past connected to now (experience, change, duration with for/since). Present Perfect Continuous = ongoing action from past until now, often with for/since.

since 2021 I have lived in East Boston since 2021.
since March I have been taking extra shifts since March.

Timeline labels: Present Perfect (past) → Pres. Perf. Cont. (past)

Perfect or perfect continuous?

Look at Rosa's timeline.

  1. Look at the timeline. Which sentence is true?

    Rosa has lived in East Boston since 2022. / Rosa has worked in housekeeping for six years. / Rosa has been taking extra shifts since March.

    Answer / teacher checkc
  2. Rosa ___ in East Boston since 2021. (live)

    has lived / is living / lived

    Answer / teacher checkhas lived
  3. Rosa started in housekeeping three years ago, so she has worked there ___ three years.

    for / since

    Answer / teacher checkfor
  4. Since March, Rosa ___ (take) extra shifts every week.
    Answer / teacher checkhas been taking

Unscramble

  1. Unscramble:
    Answer / teacher checkRosa has worked in housekeeping for three years

Future Plans, Results, and Duration

Scene  116 bus toward Maverick Square. Thursday, 6:15 PM. Photo: Aleksandr Popov / Unsplash

On the way to the last class, Rosa and classmate David talk on the 116 bus about their plans for the summer and the fall.

👨🏻
David
Level 4 in the fall?
👩🏽
Rosa
That’s the plan. I am going to take evening classes. I already filled out the form.
👨🏻
David
I think Level 4 will be harder. More reading.
👩🏽
Rosa
Maybe. Oh, I know! I'll ask Ms. Tran for the reading list tonight.

going to = a plan you already made. will = a prediction ("I think...") or a decision you make right now.

plan I am going to take evening classes in the fall.
prediction I think Level 4 will be harder.
decide now Oh, I know! I'll ask Ms. Tran tonight.

Review from W32 and W35. These are forms you have already practiced.

Completed result: By August, I will have finished the summer course.

Duration: By June, we will have been studying together for about nine months.

Optional preview only: future continuous. At 7 PM in September, I will be sitting in class. This describes an activity in progress at a future time. It is not part of the required quiz.

Timeline labels: will (decision, prediction) (future) → going to (plan) (future)

Want a head start?: For optional reference, open the Future Simple (app reference), Future Continuous (app reference), Future Perfect (app reference), or All Tenses Overview (app reference) full guides.

Bring back Weeks 32 and 35

  1. By Friday, I ___ (finish) my plan. Use the future perfect.
    Answer / teacher checkwill have finished
  2. By June, I ___ (study) here for about nine months. Use the future perfect continuous.
    Answer / teacher checkwill have been studying

Will or going to?

Read the clue in each sentence, then choose.

  1. Rosa filled out the Level 4 form last week. In September she ___ evening classes. (take)

    is going to take / takes / has taken

    Answer / teacher checkis going to take
  2. David is guessing. "I think Level 4 ___ harder." (be)

    is being / will be / was

    Answer / teacher checkwill be
  3. Rosa decides right now: "Oh, I know! I ___ (ask) Ms. Tran tonight." Use a short form.
    Answer / teacher check'll ask,will ask

Review: completed by a future date

Review the difference between a completed result and a duration.

  1. "By August, I will have finished the summer course." When does Rosa finish the course?

    No later than the start of August / In September / She never finishes it

    Answer / teacher checka
  2. "By June, I will have been studying for about nine months." What does this emphasize?

    A completed homework task / The duration of studying up to June / A new activity starting in July

    Answer / teacher checkb

Find the error

  1. "I <strong>going to</strong> enroll in Level 4 in September."

    Correct as written / Should be 'I am going to enroll' / Should be 'I will going to enroll'

    Answer / teacher checkam going to

Guide mini-quiz

  1. Rosa is texting the babysitter at work right now. Which sentence fits?

    She texts the babysitter at work. / She is texting the babysitter at work. / She has texted the babysitter at work.

    AnswerShe is texting the babysitter at work.

    Present continuous for an action in progress right now.

  2. Find the error: "I have lived here since 2021."

    No error. / Error: should be 'lived' (past simple). / Error: should be 'am living' (present continuous).

    AnswerNo error.

    Present perfect with 'since' connects a past start to now.

  3. Fill in the blank: "Rosa ___ class every Tuesday and Thursday." (It's her regular schedule.)
    Answertakes

    Present simple for routines and fixed schedules.

  4. Rosa finished her homework, and then the bus came. Which sentence fits?

    She had already finished her homework when the bus came. / She already finishes her homework when the bus came. / She has already finished her homework when the bus came.

    AnswerShe had already finished her homework when the bus came.

    Past perfect for something finished before another past event.

  5. Rosa already filled out the Level 4 form. Put the words in order.
    AnswerShe is going to take evening classes in September

    Going to is for a plan that is already decided. Rosa filled out the form, so the plan is made.

  6. I ___ (work) for two hours when my break started. Use the past perfect continuous.
    Answerhad been working

    The complete verb phrase is had been working.

  7. By Friday, I ___ (finish) my plan. Use the future perfect.
    Answerwill have finished

    The complete verb phrase is will have finished.

  8. By June, I ___ (study) here for about nine months. Use the future perfect continuous.
    Answerwill have been studying

    The complete verb phrase is will have been studying.

Week 36 Bonus Quiz 1 · optional
  1. steal → V1-s (he/she/it)
    Answersteals

    V1-s (he/she/it) of steal: steals.

  2. steal → V-ing
    Answerstealing

    V-ing of steal: stealing.

  3. steal → V2 (past)
    Answerstole

    V2 (past) of steal: stole.

  4. steal → V3 (past participle)
    Answerstolen

    V3 (past participle) of steal: stolen.

  5. freeze → V1-s (he/she/it)
    Answerfreezes

    V1-s (he/she/it) of freeze: freezes.

  6. freeze → V-ing
    Answerfreezing

    V-ing of freeze: freezing.

  7. freeze → V2 (past)
    Answerfroze

    V2 (past) of freeze: froze.

  8. freeze → V3 (past participle)
    Answerfrozen

    V3 (past participle) of freeze: frozen.

  9. Someone ___ my bike last year. (steal)
    Answerstole

    Someone stole my bike last year. (steal)

  10. The water has ___ overnight. (freeze)
    Answerfrozen

    The water has frozen overnight. (freeze)

  11. This English class offers many opportunities for personal _____.

    achievement / growth / goal / commitment

    Answergrowth

    growth: getting better over time. This job offers many opportunities for personal growth.

  12. Which word means “feeling sure of yourself”?

    confident / goal / achievement

    Answerconfident

    confident: feeling sure of yourself. She feels confident that she will pass the exam.

  13. Rosa already filled out the Level 4 form. Put the words in order. Words: She / is / going / to / take / evening / classes / in / September
    AnswerShe is going to take evening classes in September

    Going to is for a plan that is already decided. Rosa filled out the form, so the plan is made.

  14. I ___ (work) for two hours when my break started. Use the past perfect continuous.
    Answerhad been working

    The complete verb phrase is had been working.
